title: Pre-Departure Information
text: Pre-Departure Information - Pre-Departure for International Undergraduates: Pay the SEVIS Fee The U.S. Department of Homeland Security requires that all F-1 visa applicants pay a nonrefundable US$350 SEVIS Fee at least three days before they apply for a visa. You can find more information about the SEVIS Fee by visiting: http://www.wichita.edu/SEVIS . Take a Complimentary F-1 Visa Preparation Course . Disclaimer: This complimentary course is offered by Catalyst GEM, an independent third-party provider. Wichita State University does not endorse, administer, or assume responsibility for the course content, services, or outcomes. Participation is voluntary, and all inquiries or concerns should be addressed directly to Catalyst GEM. Apply for a Student Visa Take a Complimentary F-1 Visa Preparation Course . Disclaimer: This complimentary course is offered by Catalyst GEM, an independent third-party provider. Wichita State University does not endorse, administer, or assume responsibility for the course content, services, or outcomes. Participation is voluntary, and all inquiries or concerns should be addressed directly to Catalyst GEM. Most student will need to obtain an F-1 visa (student visa). We strongly recommend applying from your country of citizenship or residence. Depending on the country, obtaining a visa can range from being quite easy to very difficult. To apply for a F-1 student visa, you must submit the following to the U.S. Embassy or Consulate: 1) Form DS-160 (completed online) FAQs About Completing the DS-160 2) Nonrefundable US$185 visa application fee. 3) Receipt* that you paid the US$350 nonrefundable SEVIS fee. *Make sure to keep the receipt and bring it with you to the U.S. 4) A passport valid for at least 6 months (plus any old passports you may have) 5) A current Form I-20 from Wichita State University 6) A photo (Visit: http://travel.state.gov/content/visas/english/general/photos.html for details) 7) Evidence of sufficient funds to study in the U.S. including a bank statement 8) U.S. Visa requirements differ from country to country, find visa information for your country by visiting: http://www.usembassy.gov/ A $250 visa integrity fee may be required at the time of visa issuance. More information about this fee is forthcoming. Check out our Visa Interview Tips at https://www.wichita.edu/VisaTips Apply to Live On-Campus All first-year students, including undergraduate international students and Intensive English students (unless otherwise eligible for an exemption under provision two of this policy statement), must live in Shocker Hall, The Suites, or The Flats during their first two semesters at Wichita State University. First-year students who meet one or more of the following criteria are exempt from living on campus: 1) Twenty-one (21) years of age or older. 2) Transferring 24 or more credit hours. 3) Married and living with spouse. 4) Living with an approved relative (parent/legal guardian, grandparent, aunt or uncle) We recommend that you make a housing reservation before coming to Wichita. We require new International Students to arrive at WSU before the residence halls officially open for the semester. If you are living in Shocker Hall, The Flats, or The Suites you must email housing@wichita.edu to let them know when you plan to move into your room so they can prepare it as an early arrival. Apply for Housing Buy an Airline Ticket (Important Dates to Know) The Wichita airport is called Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport (airport code ICT). If you are coming from a country outside of the U.S., you will have at least one connecting flight before arriving in Wichita. We suggest you allow for at least a 3-hour layover in your first arrival city in the U.S. so that you have sufficient time for immigration processing, customs inspection, and a required security check before your connecting flight leaves for Wichita. Please refer to these important dates when you book your air tickets: Important Dates Summer Session 2026 Fall Semester 2026 October Session 2026 Spring Semester 2027 March Session 2027 Recommended Arrival Date May 24 (Sun) –May 26 (Tue) Aug 09(Sun) –Aug 11 (Tue) Oct 9 (Fri) –Oct 11 (Sun) Jan 10 (Sun) –Jan 12 (Tue) Mar 14 (Sun) –Mar 16(Tue) Earliest Date Allowed to Enter the U.S. Apr 26 (Sun) Jul 12 (Sun) Sep 12 (Fri) Dec 14 (Mon) Feb 14 (Sun) First Day of Classes Jun 1 (Mon) Aug 17 (Mon) Oct 14 (Wed) Jan 19 (Tue) Mar 22 (Mon) Last Day of Finals July 24 (Fri) Dec 10 (Thu) Dec 10 (Thu) May 13(Thu) May 13 (Thu) * Note: The university will be closed for winter holiday, starting at the end of the day on Friday December 18, 2026, through January 3, 2027. The university will reopen Monday, January 4, 2027. We offer FREE airport transportation from the Wichita airport during recommended arrival days. If you would like to request free pick-up from the airport, fill out the form at: https://www.wichita.edu/arrival at least 48 hours before your scheduled arrival. We only provide rides from Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport and will not provide pickups from any other airport. You can choose to take a taxi or Uber/Lyft to the University, taxi fare is approximately US$30-$40. If you arrive late and did not arrange airport pickup, you may have to stay in a hotel for one night at your own expense. There are many hotels near the airport that cost approximately US$90 - US$120 per night. Arrive on Campus (Check-In) You will receive further email communication from our office regarding check-in procedures approximately one month before the start of classes or when we receive notification of your student visa approval. Check-in is required before you are able to enroll in your classes. Failure to properly follow check-in procedures will delay your enrollment. You will need your passport and I-20 (if you are on an F-1 visa) to check-in. If you did not submit official paper transcripts when you applied for admission, please bring your official final transcripts with you to Wichita and submit these physical documents to the Office of International Education. They will be returned to you. For details on our transcript requirements, visit: http://wichita.edu/CountryRequirements . All University offices are open Monday - Friday from 8:00am to 5:00pm, with the exception of holidays. Offices are closed on Saturdays and Sundays. Open a Bank Account After arriving in Wichita, you may open a bank account. We have popular banks nearby - Campus Credit Union at the Rhatigan Student Center (RSC), Meritrust Credit Union at Braeburn Square on campus, and Bank of America has a branch next to our campus. Most of these banks have an ATM located in the RSC. In order to open an account, you will need to show the bank your passport, your I-20, and proof of your address in Wichita (such as your housing contract or apartment rental contract). You will receive an ATM card after opening an account so you can get cash quickly and easily. Know the Cost of Your Education The cost listed on your I-20 is an estimate. Actual cost of tuition and fees will depend on your major and the number of classes you take. The amount you owe will be posted in your WSU student account. Actual housing expenditures depend on: 1) the residence hall or apartment in which you live, 2) whether or not you have a roommate, and 3) your meal plan. You should bring extra money for personal expenses (such as shopping, entertainment, etc). Check out undergraduate tuition and fee estimates at http://www.wichita.edu/UGExpenses or Intensive English tuition and fees at http://www.wichita.edu/IEExpenses . Pay Tuition and Fees Students are not required to pay their tuition and fees before coming to Wichita. Tuition, fees, and housing payments are charged on a semester-by-semester basis. Deadline for payment is usually two weeks after school starts. There are several options to make payment to the university: Direct Deposit from U.S. Bank Account : After you open a bank account in the U.S., you can setup direct deposit from your U.S. bank account to your student account at WSU. Electronic Bank Transfer : Wichita State University uses a payment platform called Flywire to process international payments via wire transfers. Please visit our website for details of wire transfers . Check, Bank Draft, Money Order, or Traveler’s Checks : If you bring a check or bank draft with you to Wichita, it is very important that the check be made payable to “Wichita State University” (and not to you). Your check should include the address of the bank in the U.S. for collections. If the check is made payable to you, you may not be able to use the money for 1-2 weeks after the check is deposited to your bank in the U.S. If your check is for an amount that exceeds what you owe, any extra amount will be applied to your next semester’s tuition and will not be refunded to you. NOTE: For any student who does not have an existing bank account or has been restricted to pay by personal check, for your convenience you can take your cash and get a cashier’s check at the Campus Credit Union (located next to the University Police Department). Let them know that the cashier’s check is for payment of your tuition, fees, or housing so that you will not be charged a fee. Credit Card : If you use a credit card to pay for your tuition, fees, medical insurance, or housing, a nonrefundable 3% service fee will be added to domestic transactions and 4.25% for international transactions. Credit cards are accepted online only. Debit Card - VISA, MasterCard : Payment is made online only by going to the Student Account Suite . To avoid the 3% - 4.25% fee associated with credit card payments, we encourage you to pay using electronic check process by entering the bank routing and account number attached to the debit card. Debit card payments cannot be made to a cashier in the Accounts Receivable office. Installment Payment Plan : This allows you to pay for your tuition and fees in smaller installments each semester. With this plan, you can make a nonrefundable payment of US$130 (which includes a US$30 administrative fee) before the payment deadline in each semester. After the initial payment of US$130, the balance will be split into three equal installments due on the 15th of each month. You can arrange the Payment Plan by logging into your WSU student account. Watch Money Matters Video Learn about Health Matters Wichita State University requires international students to have medical insurance. You will be automatically charged for medical insurance unless you can provide proof of medical insurance coverage from another provider that meets U.S. Affordable Care Act benefit requirements. A tuberculin (TB) blood test is required for all new students and is given by WSU’s Student Health Service. Please bring your vaccination records with you to the U.S. If you need any vaccinations when you arrive, your student health insurance will cover them and you can get them at Student Health. We recommend that you take care of any existing medical or dental problems at home since student medical insurance does not cover routine dental work or eye examinations. Medical Insurance: https://wichita.edu/medicalinsurance Testing and Routine Medical Care: https://wichita.edu/TB Stay Connected Stay up-to-date with the fun things that are happening at the WSU International Education Office by following our Facebook and Instagram! Like our Facebook @WichitaStateInternational Follow on Instagram @WichitaStateInternational INTERNATIONAL GRADUATE STUDENTS: Please refer to the Pre-Departure Information that was sent to you with your admission letter and I-20. Find detailed Pre-Departure Information for: 2025-2026 Pre-Departure Packing Guideline

title: Location and Weather
text: Location and Weather - Location & Weather City and State City Population: 630,000 Size in Area: 423 sq km Campus to Airport: 20 minutes Wichita is the largest city in Kansas. It is the cultural, industrial, and financial center of Kansas. The city has a top-rated symphony orchestra, ballet, beautiful parks, and interesting museums. More than 800 corporations conduct international trade in the city and Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport (ICT) is one of the fastest-growing airports in the nation. Wichita is known for its warm and friendly people, good schools, and low crime rate. The city has been given the prestigious All-American City award three times. This award is given to the 10 best cities in the U.S. Kansas has also been cited as being the 4th most livable state in America because of its attractive employment opportunities, quality education, affordable housing, and strong economy. Weather Wichita enjoys four seasons a year. Spring has mild temperatures and the city receives rain more often during this season than any other time of the year. Thousands of flowers bloom on the campus during the spring. Summer is hot and somewhat humid with bright and sunny days. Fall has mild temperatures and the city is especially colorful during this season. Winter is our coldest season and light snowfall occurs every few weeks. title: ACIREMA Workshop
text: ACIREMA Workshop - ACIREMA Workshop What is ACIREMA? ACIREMA (America spelled backwards) is a workshop that includes a simulation exercise designed to sensitize participants to the months of difficulties that international students encounter in their quest for a U.S. education. It acquaints the participants with the procedures and obstacles students must follow from the initial contact with a U.S. educational institution to their arrival on campus. A facilitated discussion takes place after the simulation to address the specific issues at stake, as well as what participants can do in the future to help support international students at Wichita State University. Workshop Schedule Dates: Friday, April 1, 2022 Time: 12:15 - 1:45 p.m., 12:30 - 2 p.m., 12:45 - 2:15 p.m., 1 - 2:30 p.m. Location: Rhatigan Student Center, 2nd floor, Room 226 Pike Room The Friday, April 1 ACIREMA Workshop is now full. ACIREMA is also hosted in the fall during International Education Week. If you are unable to join us this time, we would love to see you at our next event! For additional information email fai.tai@wichita.edu

title: J-1 Exchange Visitors
text: J-1 Exchange Visitors - Bringing Exchange Visitors to Wichita State When completing required forms, download the form and open it in Adobe Acrobat. Do not fill out the forms directly in your browser. STEP 1 The prospective Exchange Visitor should make initial contact with an academic department at WSU. STEP 2 If the department is interested in potentially hosting the visitor, the department should request the prospective Exchange Visitor to complete an Exchange Visitor Application . For more information about the different categories of exchange visitors that WSU is approved to host, please visit www.wichita.edu/J-1categories . STEP 3 The prospective visitor should complete the Exchange Visitor Application and return it to the department with the following documents: Dependent Information for Exchange Visitors Form (if bringing dependents) Passport copies for exchange visitor and any dependents Sponsorship documentation (if being sponsored by a university, government, or organization) Copy of diploma or any English test scores from Part D of the Exchange Visitor Application Curriculum Vitae (CV) or résumé STEP 4 The department reviews the application and supporting documents to determine if they would like to host the visitor. STEP 5 If the WSU department decides to host the visitor, the DS-2019 Request Form must be completed. After Parts A-E have been completed, the department chair will need to initial by each number in Part F (numbers 9-20 are only required for the student intern category) and sign in Part G. In order to complete the form, the department must determine if it will financially sponsor the visitor and, if so, the amount of sponsorship. In addition, the department must obtain evidence that the Exchange Visitor has sufficient English to participate in the exchange program. The department will need to conduct an interview with the exchange visitor and complete the J-1 English Proficiency Evaluation if the visitor does not have other acceptable evidence of English proficiency. See the DS-2019 Request Form for more details. As part of the DS-2019 Request Form, the department will also need to draft the department invitation letter. A link to a sample invitation letter can be found on the DS-2019 Request Form. The invitation letter should not be shared with the exchange visitor until the given department has been granted approval to do so (Step 8). The university offers instructions for Adobe Digital Signatures here . STEP 6 The department should print all documents and send them to the college dean for approval. The documents should include: DS-2019 Request Form Department Invitation Letter ( Sample) J-1 English Proficiency Evaluation (if used to verify English proficiency) with list of interview questions, if applicable Exchange Visitor Application Dependent Information for Exchange Visitors Form (if visitor is bringing dependents) Passport copies for exchange students and any dependents Sponsorship documentation (if visitor is being sponsored by an outside university, government, or organization) Copy of diploma or any English test scores (if used to verify English proficiency) Curriculum Vitae (CV) or résumé STEP 7 The college dean will review all documentation. If approved, the dean will sign the DS-2019 Request Form and forward the documentation on for the next approval signature according to the instructions in Part G of the DS-2019 Request Form. Ultimately, the documents will be reviewed and approved by the Office of Export Controls and Compliance, the Office of General Counsel, and the Office of Academic Affairs before finally being sent to Tonya Baldwin at the Office of International Education. STEP 8 Tonya Baldwin will email the department to notify them that the exchange visitor request has been approved and that the department can share the invitation letter with the exchange visitor. STEP 9 (Student Intern category only) If the visitor will be coming under the Student Intern category, the department must also complete the Form DS-7002, Training/Internship Placement Plan . See the Guide to Form DS-7002 for details on how to complete the form. The department should send the completed Form DS-7002, Training/Internship Placement Plan to the visitor to sign. The exchange visitor should provide a copy of this document to his/her home institution and request that the institution complete the Home Institution Certification Form . The exchange visitor should send the signed DS-7002 and the completed Home Institution Certification Form to Tonya Baldwin in the Office of International Education at tonya.baldwin@wichita.edu . STEP 10 Tonya Baldwin will email the exchange visitor (and copy the department) the following: A Certification of Financial Support for the exchange visitor to sign and return with, if applicable, evidence of financial support. Information about purchasing WSU medical insurance. STEP 11 Once Tonya Baldwin receives the completed Certification of Financial Support and funds for the WSU medical insurance, she will prepare the Form DS-2019 and send it to the department or directly to the exchange visitor as indicated on DS-2019 Request Form. For visitors coming under the Student Intern category, the Office of International Education will also send the final DS-7002 signed by the Responsible Officer. STEP 12 The exchange visitor pays the I-901 SEVIS fee and applies for a J-1 visa. After obtaining a visa, the visitor should make arrangements to come to WSU.
reason: clear step-by-step instructions for bringing exchange visitors to WSU

title: Wichita State University / Autonomous University of Chihuahua
text: Wichita State University / Autonomous University of Chihuahua - Wichita State University / Autonomous University of Chihuahua Dual Degree Program INTRODUCTION Wichita State University (WSU) is excited about the possibility of developing a dual degree program with the Autonomous University of Chihuahua (Universidad Autónoma de Chihuahua or UACH). To explore if this type of agreement is possible, WSU must first conduct a thorough transfer credit evaluation to determine if the classes taken at UACH are equivalent to classes offered at WSU. In order to begin an evaluation, please follow the steps below: STEP 1 - GATHER SYLLABI FOR CLASSES THAT YOU WOULD LIKE US TO EVALUATE Because of the differences between the educational system in Mexico and the U.S., we must have syllabi (in English) for all classes that students would typically take at UACH as part of the dual degree program. The syllabi should include as much detailed information as possible about the material studied in each subject as well as the amount of time spent in lectures and laboratories. Example of a Syllabus STEP 2 - COLLECT A TYPICAL UACH TRANSCRIPT It is helpful for us to have a typical transcript from UACH so that we can see grades (and a grading scale), course numbers, and credit hours/units (if applicable). The transcript should be in English. STEP 3 - PROVIDE YOUR SCHOOL CALENDAR When conducting an evaluation, it will be helpful for us to know the months during which classes are normally in session at UACH. For this reason, please provide your school's academic calendar. STEP 4 - SEND THE ABOVE ITEMS TO WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY Please send the above items to Ms. Michelle Barger at intltransfer.eval@wichita.edu or post to: Ms. Michelle Barger Office of International Education Wichita State University 1845 Fairmount Street Wichita, Kansas 67260-0122 USA Telephone: +1-316-978-3232 STEP 5 - DETERMINATION OF COURSE EQUIVALENCIES After you have provided all of the items in Steps 1 to 3, Wichita State University will begin a transfer credit evaluation. This process involves our sending the UACH syllabus for each subject to the WSU department which offers a comparable class. STEP 6 - DEGREE AUDIT EVALUATION AND CREATION OF STUDY PLANS After Step 5 is complete, we will use this information to determine which UACH classes meet the degree requirements for the majors included in our agreement. This process is called a degree audit. It is important to note that not all of the classes that a student completed previously, even if they are comparable to subjects offered at WSU, may satisfy the degree requirements for a particular major at WSU. For example, if a student took a math class at your school and we determined that it is equivalent to an Algebra class offered at WSU, Algebra would meet a degree requirement for many majors at WSU -- but not necessarily for Engineering majors. A degree audit evaluation will determine the number of subjects (and approximate amount of time) required for a student to complete their degree at WSU. Wichita State University is interested in pursuing dual degree programs for the following majors offered at WSU: Liberal Arts and Sciences • Bachelor’s Degree in Chemistry • Bachelor of Communication Sciences • Bachelor of Arts in Hispanic American Literature Barton School of Business • Bachelor of Business Administration • Bachelor of International Business College of Fine Arts • Bachelor of Visual Arts • Bachelor’s degree in Audiovisual Production College of Engineering • Bachelor of Aerospace Engineering • Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Process Engineering NOTE: If a UACH student is interested in pursuing a major at WSU that is not listed above, we would be happy to consider the student for admission and conduct an individualized degree audit for that particular student. The student would then know how long it will take to graduate from Wichita State University with a major that is not included in our agreement.
reason: Clear step-by-step instructions for dual degree program evaluation and detailed information on majors offered

title: Transfer Students

title: International Students FAQ
text: International Students FAQ - Frequently Asked Questions from International Students Before Applying Money Matters Submitting an Application Conditional Admission English Requirements After Admission/Pre-departure After Arrival Before Applying 1. Can I find out if I will be accepted before I apply for admission? No. Pre-evaluation of documents are not given before you apply for admission. You must formally apply for admission and submit the required application materials before your application will be evaluated. Students are encouraged to review our admission requirements to see if they are likely to be eligible for admission. 2. Is admission guaranteed if I apply and submit all required documents? No. Wichita State University cannot guarantee admission. An admission decision is determined based on the evaluation of a student’s application and related documents. 3. Can I email application materials such as transcripts, test scores, etc.? The preferred method of submitting application materials is through your personal application status portal . This is a secure way to submit all of your application materials. 4. Can I find out how many credits will transfer from my previous school before I apply? Evaluation of transfer credits does not begin until you have applied and are accepted for admission to Wichita State University. The process of evaluating transfer credit can take up to two months to complete depending on how many credits you request to transfer. Please plan accordingly. For additional information regarding how transfer credit from international schools is awarded, please click here . If you are seeking transfer credit from some U.S. universities or an American Degree Transfer Program, you may be able to estimate how many of your credits will transfer by using our transfer gateway portal . Please note that this portal does not necessarily contain a comprehensive list of every course at every school, only those that have been previously evaluated. 5. What is the minimum GPA required for admission? The undergraduate minimum GPA requirement for admission is 2.5 on a 4.0 grading scale or the international equivalent. GPA is not the only factor taken into consideration when a student applies. If a student does not meet the minimum GPA requirement for admission, they can submit SAT or ACT scores for consideration instead. Students must formally apply and submit transcripts and/or test scores in order for the Office of International Education to determine if they are eligible for admission to Wichita State. GPA requirements for admission to the Graduate School vary by major and range from 2.75 - 3.00 on a 4.0 grading scale. 6. Can I apply with a 3-Year Bachelor's Degree? 3-year degrees are accepted for admission to some graduate programs . Pre-evaluations are not available. Interested students must formally apply for graduate admission to find out if their 3-year degree will be accepted for their program of interest. Admission requirements vary by program. For information on acceptable 3-year bachelor’s degrees, please contact the graduate school at wsugradschool@wichita.edu . 7. How long will it take to complete my degree/program? Undergraduate Most bachelor's degrees require about 4 years to complete. This estimate depends on how many credit hours a student takes per semester. Students who wish to graduate in the estimated 4 years should take at least 15 credit hours per semester. Students will also meet with an academic advisor to decide their plan of study. Intensive English There are 7 levels of Intensive English. Each level lasts 8 weeks or approximately half an academic semester. The length of time a student studies in Intensive English depends on the individual’s level of English proficiency at the beginning of their study. Graduate Most graduate programs will last about 2 years, but the actual duration depends on a student’s personal plan of study. 8. What are the minimum/maximum number of credit hours I can transfer to Wichita State? Undergraduate There is no minimum number of credit hours you can transfer to Wichita State. The maximum number of credit hours you can transfer is 60 from a 2-year college or 90 credit hours from a 4-year university. Note that it is not guaranteed that all of your transfer credits will apply toward your intended degree program at Wichita State. Graduate Please contact the Graduate School for more information about transfer credit for graduate degree level coursework. 9. Can I apply before I graduate from high school? Yes. You can apply for admission to Wichita State before you finish high school. Most students will begin applying to universities approximately one year or one semester before they intend to graduate from high school. Once you complete your high school education, our office will ask for final scores and/or grades to confirm you still meet Wichita State’s standards for admission. 10. Is a GRE or GMAT required for my graduate application? GRE or GMAT is required for some graduate programs in order to apply for admission. View admission requirements for your program of interest. 11. Is a SAT or ACT score required to apply? No. You are not required to take an SAT or ACT to apply, but is an option for Freshman Admission . SAT or ACT scores can also be used for determining English proficiency and beginning coursework in Math and English if you are admitted to Wichita State. If you have these scores, we encourage you to request them be sent to Wichita State University. Back to Top Money Matters 1. Can I have an application fee waiver? No, Wichita State University does not provide application fee waivers. Applications and related materials will not be considered without an application fee. Wichita State University understands currency exchange is difficult in certain countries, however, submission of an application fee is still required. The application fee cannot be paid after you get admission or after you arrive. 2. How do I pay the application fee if I don’t have a credit card? Undergraduate or Intensive English: Students who are unable to pay by credit card can use our payment partner, Flywire , to pay their application fee. Graduate: View information about the graduate application fee. 3. Why am I being asked to pay an application fee when I already paid through CommonApp? It can take Wichita State University several days to receive application fee payments made through CommonApp. Please allow up to one week for your application fee payment to be received. 4. Why is my payment through Flywire not showing in my student account? Flywire allows students/payers to track the status of their payment. It can take 1-2 days for the university to reconcile payments and post to your student account after the payment is received from Flywire. 5. What financial documents do I need to apply? Undergraduate or Intensive English: The Certification of Financial Support Form must be submitted with all applications. An instructional video walking through how to complete a Certification of Financial Support can be found here . Bank statements or other financial documents will also accompany this form and are required. A list of acceptable financial documents can be found here . Graduate: The Graduate Certification of Financial Support Form must be submitted with all graduate applications. Instructions for completing this form are on the form. 6. What is the estimated cost of attendance? An updated cost estimate is released every academic year. Exact cost estimates for a full 4-year degree are not available, as there are too many variables that may influence the cost of your education over a 4 years. Undergraduate: View Costs Intensive English: View Costs Graduate: View Costs 7.Can you tell me what the exact cost of my bill will be? No. We cannot give an exact cost for any student’s studies at Wichita State University. The exact cost of study will depend on your major, what classes you take, and how many classes you take each semester. Please review our estimated costs for a general idea of the expected costs for the current academic year. Undergraduate Costs Intensive English Costs Graduate Costs 8. How much funding do I need to show the U.S. Embassy? Undergraduate or Intensive English: See the amount shown on your personalized Certification of Financial Support Form . This is the minimum amount the U.S. Embassy will expect to see. Graduate: See the amount shown on your personalized Graduate Certification of Financial Support Form . This is the minimum amount the U.S. Embassy will expect to see. 9. Is an enrollment deposit required? An enrollment deposit is required for applicants from Nigeria , Democratic Republic of Congo , Fujian, China , and Bangladesh before an I-20 will be sent. The payment of an enrollment deposit improves chances of being granted a visa in these countries or provinces. If desired, students who are not from one of the four countries or provinces above may pay tuition in advance to improve chances of receiving a visa. The student may choose the amount they wish to pay. Learn about payment options here . View Wichita State University's policy for the refund of enrollment deposits and advanced tuition . 10. What is Wichita State University’s bank account information? Wichita State University does not share its bank account information. To send payments to the university, students should use our international payment portal, Flywire , to make payments in local currency or in U.S. dollars through bank transfer or credit card. In countries that require government approval to send money to the U.S., Flywire helps students prepare required forms and paperwork for payment. If you have questions about the payment process you may reach out to the Flywire customer support team at support@flywire.com for assistance. 11. What scholarships and financial aid are available? As a U.S. public university, Wichita State does not offer full scholarships. Please view links to scholarships and other financial aid opportunities below. Undergraduate: Global Select Scholarship *most popular* Scholarships and other Financial Aid Intensive English: Not eligible for scholarship assistance. Graduate: Assistantships Graduate School Awards Global Select Scholarship 12. What are my job opportunities while in the United States? Wichita State University has 250+ unique employers on-campus. There are many immigration laws that determine an international student’s work eligibility in the United States. Please review the information below to learn about your work eligibility while in the U.S. Employment Information for Undergraduate or Intensive English students Learn about graduate assistantships 13. Do I need to pay the full amount of my tuition all at once? No. Wichita State University offers a payment plan for students where they may pay their tuition in installments. A US$30 administrative fee is charged for the set-up of the payment plan. Students cannot apply for a payment plan until after arriving in Wichita and enrolling in classes, which will determine the total cost of tuition for the semester. Amount of payments cannot be calculated prior to the selection of classes. Housing expenses are not included in the tuition payment plan. IMPORTANT: You must choose to enroll in the payment plan each semester. This is not done automatically. Visit your Student Account Suite in your myWSU portal under the myFinances tab to enroll in and set-up the payment plan option. Payment schedule: Fall Semester: First payment due in August after selecting classes then September 15, October 15, and November 15. Spring Semester: First payment due in January after selecting classes then February 15, March 15, and April 15. Summer Session: First payment due in June after selecting classes then July 15 14. Are graduate assistantships available? Wichita State University provides assistantships to graduate students each year. However, graduate assistantships cannot be guaranteed. All students must submit an assistantship application to be considered. Learn more 15. What is the SEVIS fee and how do I pay? The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) requires people who want F-1 or J-1 visas to pay a one-time SEVIS Fee before applying for a visa. Get more information about the SEVIS fee including how to pay here . 16. Can I get a refund? We provide a detailed refund policy regarding the payment of advanced tuition, application fees, and enrollment deposits. View Details Back to Top Submitting an Application 1. How do I apply? Undergraduate or Intensive English: Steps to Apply Graduate: 1) Apply for Admission 2) Submit all materials required for the student's major (such as letters of recommendation, GMAT or GRE scores, etc). Admission Requirements by Major 2. What are the admission requirements? Undergraduate: Freshman Admission : Minimum GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 grading scale or international equivalent. Transfer Admission : GPA requirements vary by major. Also review our list of Required Application Materials . Graduate: View Admission Requirements by Major 3. What are the intake deadlines? Undergraduate intakes : Spring, Summer, and Fall Intensive English intakes : Spring, March, Summer, Fall, and October Graduate intakes : Spring and Fall 4. When does my semester start and end? Fall Semester: mid-August – mid-December Spring Semester: mid-January – mid-May Summer Semester: June-July Exact start and end dates for upcoming semesters can be found here . You should plan to arrive to Wichita State based on the recommended arrival dates for your intended semester found under the “Buy an Airline Ticket” heading on our pre-departure information page . 5. What majors/degrees are offered? Wichita State University offers more than 225 majors and specializations. Find the major that is right for you! Undergraduate Graduate 6. Do I need a letter of recommendation for my application? Undergraduate: Letters of recommendation are not required. Graduate: A letter of recommendation is required for a few majors. View graduate admission requirements for your program of interest to see if a letter of recommendation is required. 7. How fast will I get a decision on my application? Wichita State University offers three different service levels for our undergraduate international applicants. Each level relates to a specific application deadline. Depending on the service level you select, application processing can take anywhere from 5 weeks to 3 business days. These service levels and processing times do not apply to graduate applications, as graduate applications are processed by Wichita State University’s Graduate School. View Details 8. How can I get updates on the status of my application? Undergraduate: After we review your application, we will automatically send an e-mail message to you to let you know your application status. In our message, we will let you know if you have been accepted, denied, or if we are missing any required application materials. We will also send you periodic reminders and other correspondence by e-mail. For this reason, it is VERY important that you check your e-mail often for updates from Wichita State University. You can also check your application status at any time through your application status portal . Graduate: For updates on your graduate application, please contact the Graduate School or view your application status portal. 9. How can I send my test scores? Undergraduate: English test scores: Can be submitted to our Office of International Education and we will verify your score with your testing company. Certain test scores must be submitted directly from the testing agency, such as Duolingo English Test scores. SAT scores: To be considered official, SAT score reports must be received from College Board. All other test scores: Please review our requirements for your country here . Graduate: Please review the graduate school application checklist to determine how your test scores should be submitted. Back to Top Conditional Admission & English Proficiency 1. What does it mean if I receive conditional admission? Students who receive conditional admission to Wichita State University meet our academic requirements for admission, but DO NOT meet our English proficiency requirement for admission to an academic program or have not submitted an English proficiency score. Students with conditional admission receive an I-20 listing Intensive English as their area of study and their academic major. Students who wish to receive an I-20 listing only their academic program should submit an approved English test score . Undergraduate: If granted Conditional Admission, you must sit for the English Proficiency Exam (EPE) after arrival in Wichita, if no other acceptable English test score is submitted. If you pass, you will begin full-time academic study in your major. If you do not pass, you must study in Intensive English until you meet the undergraduate English requirement . Graduate: If you have not met our English requirement, you MUST apply for both graduate admission AND to Intensive English. No I-20 will be issued until: 1) You submit an approved English test score that meets the English proficiency requirement. OR 2) You apply to Intensive English . You must meet our English requirement before beginning graduate classes. If the GMAT or GRE is required for admission, official scores must be submitted before an admission is made. Please review the graduate admission requirements for your program of interest to see if a GMAT or GRE score is required for admission. 2. What is your English requirement? Undergraduate: Ways to Demonstrate English Proficiency Graduate: TOEFL iBT : 79 for most majors IELTS : 6.5 for most majors View majors with a higher English requirement . Test scores must be sent to Wichita State directly from the testing company. 3. Do I have to apply to your ESL program? Undergraduate: If you have met the undergraduate English requirement, you do not need to apply to Intensive English. If you have not met the English requirement before arriving at Wichita State, you are not automatically required to apply to Intensive English. If you have not met our English requirement by the time you arrive in Wichita, we will test your English before you begin classes. If you pass our English test, you will begin full-time study in your academic major. If you do not pass, you will be required to study in Intensive English. Graduate: If you have met the graduate English requirement, you do not need to apply to Intensive English. However, if you have not met the English Requirement at the time you apply for graduate admission, you should apply to Intensive English as well. The Graduate School will not issue and I-20 until: 1) You submit an approved English test score that meets the English proficiency requirement. OR 2) You apply to Intensive English . Your I-20 will be for Intensive English and not your academic major. Back to Top After Admission & Pre-departure 1. Do I need to receive any vaccinations before I travel to the U.S.? International travelers are NOT required to show proof of full COVID-19 vaccination prior to boarding their flight to the United States. View Details If you plan to live in one of Wichita State University’s residence halls, you must be vaccinated for meningitis. We recommend that you get the meningitis vaccine before coming to the U.S. If you get the vaccine in your country, you must bring proof of your vaccination with you to the U.S. If desired, you may get the meningitis vaccine from Student Health Services. If you purchase medical insurance through WSU, you will not be charged for the vaccine. 2. What airport should I fly to? Your final destination should be Wichita, Kansas (Airport Code: ICT). For undergraduate students: After you are accepted, we will enclose Pre-Departure information with your I-20 that includes airport arrival details and recommended dates of arrival. 3. Will you come pick me up when I arrive? Yes, you can request pick-up from the airport for free. Airport pick-up cannot be guaranteed, as it is dependent on the number of volunteer drivers available. You will be notified if your request for pick-up could not be fulfilled. Please complete the airport pickup form so we know when to expect you. 4. Do I need to purchase my own medical insurance? You will be automatically charged for medical insurance unless you can provide proof of medical insurance coverage from another provider that meets U.S. Affordable Care Act benefit requirements. Learn more 5. How do I apply for on-campus housing? Follow the instructions for reserving your on-campus room by selecting “Apply Now” on Wichita State’s housing webpage . We encourage you to wait to submit your housing application until after you know if you have been granted a visa for study at Wichita State. Note: On-Campus housing is not available for married students or students with children. Married students or students with children will need to find housing accommodations off campus . 6. Can I live off-campus? All first-year students at Wichita State University are required live on campus for their first year of study. Also note that homestays are not available. Exceptions to living on-campus: 1. You plan to live with a family member who is one of the following: parent, legal guardian, aunt, uncle, or grandparent. 2. You are 21 or older. 3. You are married and/or have children you will be living with. 4. You have 24 or more transferable credit hours. Living Off-campus : Students who want to live off campus must complete a Housing Exemption request form. To access the form, log in to your myWSU portal , and select Campus Housing from the Student Tools box in the center of the screen. Next, select Manage My Forms at the top of the page and use the Form Selector to find the Exemption Request form. Fill out the rest of the request form as prompted. A Housing staff member will respond to your request within 3 business days. 7. When and where do I pay my SEVIS fee? The SEVIS Fee can be paid to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) online, by mail with a check or money order, or by Western Union. You will pay the SEVIS fee after you receive admission and before you apply for a student visa. F-1 Visas: School Code for Wichita State University: KAN214F00668000 SEVIS Identification Number: Located above the bar code on the right side of your I-20 starting with "N" J-1 Visas: Program Code: P-1-01549 SEVIS Identification Number: Located on your DS-2019 To pay your SEVIS Fee, please go to the following website for complete details: https://www.ice.gov/sevis/i901/index.htm . More information about the SEVIS fee 8. Where can I find information about what to do before I arrive? Pre-Departure information will be sent to you after you receive your I-20. This information includes when to arrive, how to apply for a visa, opening a bank account, how to pay tuition after arrival, and much more. Or office also prepares a suggested packing list. Learn More 9. Can Wichita State University help me get a visa? Wichita State University is not permitted to influence any student’s visa application process. We cannot contact the U.S. embassy on your behalf and encourage them to grant you a student visa. We do provide students with a page dedicated to tips for visa interviews . We encourage all students to review this information before a via interview. 10. When can I enroll in classes? You can enroll in classes after you complete the following steps. 1. Arrive in Wichita 2. Complete the check-in process with the Office of International Education 3. Meet with your academic advisor IMPORTANT: Arriving during our recommended arrival dates will give you plenty of time to complete all the processes necessary before you can enroll in classes. If you arrive after these dates, you will risk delaying your class enrollment for your intended semester. 11. How can I defer my admission and get a new I-20? Students who wish to defer their admission to a later term must complete the readmission process by following the instructions at www.wichita.edu/readmission . Our office must receive your readmission application and any required updated documents before issuing a new I-20. 12. Can I arrive late? U.S. Customs and Border Protection expects students to arrive no later than the program start date listed on their I-20. Wichita State’s recommended dates of arrival each semester follow this expectation. Arrival after your program start date requires written approval from Wichita State. Late arrivals are approved on a case by case basis. In general, you will not be granted late arrival approval if any of the following statements apply to your situation. 1. You have not been granted a visa interview by the U.S. embassy. 2. The visa interview date you received is scheduled for a date after the program start date and/or recommended arrival dates for your intended semester. 3. You receive your visa after the recommended arrival dates. 4. You are requesting to arrive after the first day of classes for your intended semester. Late arrivals are approved sparingly in the best interest of our students. Arriving late causes many delays that negatively impact a student’s academic performance and overall well-being. We want all students beginning their studies at Wichita State to start on the path to success. We suggest students in any of the situations above request readmission to a later semester. 13. Can I bring my parents with me while I study? Your parents will not be able to stay with you for the duration of your studies at Wichita State. They are welcome to accompany you to help you get settled in Wichita when you first arrive, or even visit you during your studies. Note that your parents will need to follow a different visa application process in order to travel with you or visit you in the United States. Contact your local U.S. embassy for more information on this process. 14. Can I bring my children and/or spouse with me while I study? Yes, it is possible to bring your children or spouse with you while you complete your studies at Wichita State. When you apply, let our office know that you intend to bring your spouse and/or child with you to the United States. You will need to show additional financial documentation to demonstrate you are able to support your dependents while in the United States. If you receive admission, our office will issue documents that will allow them to apply for a visa. Please note that visa approval for your spouse and/or children is not guaranteed, even if you receive a visa for your studies. Back to Top After Arrival 1. How do I open a bank account? After arriving in Wichita, you may choose to open a bank account. We have popular banks nearby - Meritrust Credit Union at Braeburn Square on campus and Bank of America has a branch next to our campus. These banks have ATMs located in the Rhatigan Student Center. In order to open an account, you will need to show the bank your passport, your I-20, and proof of your address in Wichita (such as your housing contract or apartment rental contract). You will receive an ATM card after opening an account so you can get cash quickly and easily. 2. How can I get in contact with other students from my country? Wichita State University has a list of university student associations . Check out the list to see if we have a student association for your country! During your student orientation you might also meet other students from your country. title: International Travel Tips
text: International Travel Tips - International Travel Tips Complete an International Travel Authorization Form so that WSU will have your contact information in the event of an emergency. Keep your cell phone and computer equipment safe by following the tips from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) , a division of the Department of Homeland Security. Check with the embassy or consulate of the countries you will be visiting to see if you will be required to have a visa. Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) , which is a free service that allows U.S. citizens to stay safe and keep informed by registering with the closest U.S. Embassy or Consulate. Make sure your passport has not expired or will not expire within six months of your expected return date to the U.S. Many countries require passports to be valid for at least six months beyond a traveler's planned return date. In addition, make sure you have plenty of blank visa pages in your passport. In the event that your passport gets lost or stolen, make a copy of your passport and any relevant visa pages and store them in a safe place. Consider making scans or taking pictures of the needed passport pages and send them to your email account so you have them, if needed. Never store your passport and the passport copies in the same location. Notify your bank and credit card company of your travel plans. To prevent your card from being used fraudulently, your bank or credit card company may automatically block any usage from outside of the U.S. Notifying your bank or credit card company in advance ensures that your card will work when needed. In case your credit card or debit card is lost or stolen, it's a good idea to write down the last four digits of each card number and the customer service telephone number located on the back of the card. IMPORTANT: In general, you cannot call toll-free telephone numbers from outside of the U.S. As such, you should use whatever telephone number that your bank or credit card company provides you for use outside of the U.S. To keep your account safe, never copy or scan your credit/debit cards. Store your bank cards and the customer service contact information in different locations. Never rely solely on the use of debit cards or credit cards during your trip. In some countries, card use is much less common than in the U.S. Be sure to have some cash available – especially if your cards are lost or stolen. Print a copy of your itinerary and hotel reservations. At some international airports, you may be required to show your itinerary in order to enter the airport check-in area. Consider purchasing a travel adapter to use with any electronics that you carry with you. Consider taking a power bank with you since power outlets are not always readily available for travelers. Check out exchange rates before you go by visiting websites such as Oanda.com . Check to see if you have received all recommended vaccinations for the countries you will be visiting. Some countries require evidence of vaccinations. Check with the embassies of the countries you're visiting to find out their vaccination requirements. Pack any prescription medications in your carry-on bags. Make sure that medications are stored in their original prescription bottles and that you carry a copy of the prescription with you in case you're questioned by a customs agent at your port of entry. Please note that some medications prescribed in the U.S. may not be legal in other countries. Visit the International Narcotics Control Board for more information. Check with your health insurance provider to see if they will provide coverage outside of the U.S. If not, consider purchasing a travel insurance policy. To determine if the water in the country you're visiting is considered safe for drinking, visit the website for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . If the water is not potable, don't use it to brush your teeth or wash fruits and vegetables. Place a hand towel over the faucet to help remind you not to use the tap water. Learn more about Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) . Students can also visit Student Health Services to obtain more information before departure. Avoid the use of narcotics. Drug offenses are punishable by death in at least 35 countries worldwide. Educate yourself about the countries you will be visiting . Familiarize yourself with local laws and customs including dress standards, photography restrictions, liquor laws, and more. Learn how to recognize culture shock and strategies to cope with it.

title: International Travel Guidelines
text: International Travel Guidelines - International Travel Guidelines To ensure compliance with federal and state export control regulations and adherence to enhanced cybersecurity measures at Wichita State, an International Travel Authorization Form must be completed by all international travelers on official university business. An International Travel Authorization Form must be completed: 1) By all international travelers at least 30 days prior to their scheduled departure date . 2) For any international travel ( business OR pleasure) which meets one or more of the following conditions: Travel being paid with WSU funds (GU, RU, Grant, Foundation, etc). Travel in which any WSU-owned hardware, software, electronic equipment, cell phones, materials, or data will be used. Travel in which you plan to connect to any WSU-owned or operated folders, files, servers, or networks. Travel that is sponsored in any way by a foreign government, foreign academic institution, or foreign entity. Travel in which you will be collaborating or receiving compensation from a foreign government, foreign academic institution, or foreign entity. Travel in which you will be receiving fringe benefits (honoraria, gifts, meals, etc) from any entity -- foreign or domestic. Travel for Study Abroad including faculty-led trips involving students. Travelers should NOT book tickets or make any travel arrangements until their travel request has been reviewed and approved. International travel requests are normally reviewed in 3 to 4 business days but may take longer in some cases. NOTE: Travel to Crimea-Region of Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, or Syria may require special approval. An export license, if required, may take several months to obtain. For this reason, plan accordingly. The International Travel Authorization Form is optional, but highly recommended, for all other international travel by faculty, staff, or students that does not meet any of the above requirements. By completing the form, WSU will have your contact information in the event of an emergency. IMPORTANT: To complete an International Travel Authorization Form, click the link below to download the form. Do NOT open the form and try to complete it in a web browser such as Chrome or Firefox. The form must be opened and completed in Acrobat Reader in order for the form to work properly. Download an International Travel Authorization Form

title: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020
text: FAQs About Enrolling for Fall 2020 - FAQs for International Students Enrolling for Fall 2020 IMPORTANT: Return often for updates Last Updated: July 27, 2020 Is it safe to study at Wichita State because of COVID-19? The Wichita metro area has not seen large numbers of COVID-19 cases like other cities have. Our hospitals and clinics are operating normally. The University is doing everything it can to keep students as safe as possible. Everyone is expected to wear face masks while on campus. Social distancing is required. You must keep at least 2 meters away from other people. To allow for social distancing, there is reduced seating capacity in classrooms, eating areas, lounges, and public areas. Public areas are sanitized at least once daily. We are here to help for our international students! We provide assistance in-person or by email, phone, WhatsApp, Zoom, or Facebook Messenger. Do I need to let you know that I plan to come to Wichita for Fall 2020? Yes! Please complete our Fall 2020 Questionnaire if you have not already done so. Complete a questionnaire AS SOON AS POSSIBLE even if you don't yet have a visa or if your plans might change later on. How will classes be taught? Because of COVID-19, classes for Fall 2020 will either be offered FULLY ONLINE or HYBRID depending on the class. Please note that new students entering the U.S. for the Fall 2020 must enroll in at least one course with an in-person component. Fully Online Classes: You may continue living where you are and take online classes for Fall 2020 without having to come to Wichita. You will be charged an extra online fee of $97.25 per credit hour when taking online classes. Hybrid Online Classes: A hybrid class often has a mixture of both in-person and online instruction. Some hybrid classes are offered completely online but the professor may require students to come to campus for exams. There is no extra fee charged for hybrid classes. Depending on the class, the content will be delivered as: 1) Asynchronous - Students can view online content and do assignments whenever it is convenient for them. OR 2) Synchronous - Students will meet in-person or online on specific days/times like you would for a traditional in-person class. For example, you might have a synchronous hybrid class that meets online on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 09:00-10:15am Central U.S. time. In this example, the professor also requires students to come to campus twice during the semester for exams. When taking a synchronous hybrid class, students should consider the class meeting time if they are living in a different time zone. In addition, the student should be aware of whether or not the professor requires students to physically come to campus for lectures or examinations. VERY IMPORTANT: Visit https://wichita.edu/Fall2020 to find out if a class is offered online or hybrid and whether the class is asynchronous or synchronous. As a new student, it is very important to look up each class to ensure that you are taking at least one course with an in-person component. What health-related matters should I take care of before coming to the U.S.? Can I receive medical care on campus after I arrive in Wichita? Student Health Sevices at Wichita State University provides a variety of medical services including routine medical examinations, laboratory services, vaccinations, prescription medications, and much more. Watch the video produced by Student Health Services to learn what new students need to know before coming to Wichita. The video also provides information about the tuberculosis (TB) testing requirement , medical insurance , and more. Learn more about mental health services available on campus. Do I have to be quarantined when I arrive? Maybe. Because all countries currently have a CDC Level 3 Travel Notice, the State of Kansas requires travelers from ALL COUNTRIES to be quarantined for 14 days starting with the day after their arrival in Kansas. In addition, Kansas requires travelers from CERTAIN U.S. STATES to be quarantined as well. Because the list of U.S. states requiring quarantine in Kansas is updated often, we won't know if you might be subject to quarantine until closer to the time that you arrive on campus. For details, visit https://www.coronavirus.kdheks.gov/175/Travel-Exposure-Related-Isolation-Quaran . Where will I quarantine? What will quarantine be like? You should begin to quarantine yourself as soon as you arrive in Kansas. Your quarantine will last for 14 days. Day 1 of your quarantine begins the morning after your arrival in Kansas. If you do not develop COVID-19 symptoms by the end of your 14 th day, you may leave quarantine without seeking permission from a health care provider or public health official. Monitor your symptoms and read the Quarantine FAQs provided by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment for travel-related quarantine. As long as you wear a mask and remain at least two meters (6 feet) away from other people, you may temporarily leave quarantine for these reasons only: ○ To seek medical attention or to obtain medication ○ To do laundry ○ To get food from a restaurant in your hotel to take back to your room to eat If you need medical assistance during your quarantine, please contact Student Health Services . If you have already set up your password in the myWSU portal, you may ask questions or schedule an appointment using the myShockerHealth portal . Otherwise, call (316) 978-4792. If you contact Student Health Services, please let them know that you are currently in travel-related quarantine. If you develop COVID-19 symptoms during quarantine, contact Student Health Services BEFORE coming to campus for medical assistance. If you need non-medical assistance during quarantine, please contact Tonya Baldwin, Assistant Director in the Office of International Education. Email: tonya.baldwin@wichita.edu | Telephone: (316) 978-6037 To learn more about how to reserve a room and get food during your quarantine , visit the FAQs provided by the Office of Housing and Residence Life . Please note the following: ○ Quarantine spaces in the residence halls on campus are very limited. Rooms are only available to students who have already signed a housing contract to live on campus. In order to get a room, students must arrive on July 25. Since this may not be possible for most international students, you will likely need to stay in a hotel during quarantine. ○ The University has obtained discount pricing for students at nearby hotels for their quarantine. Complete details about the hotels, the cost, food options, and more can be found on the above webpage. You should reserve a hotel room BEFORE coming back to Wichita so that you can go directly from the airport to your hotel room to begin your quarantine. When making a hotel reservation, let the hotel know that you are a Wichita State University student in order to get the special discount rate. ○ You are allowed to quarantine in the home of a friend or family member as long as you adhere to the requirements provided by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment . title: Important Announcements
text: Important Announcements - Important Announcement for Current International Students Release Date: July 7, 2020 The Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) has released guidance for the Fall 2020 term. This guidance is different than previous guidance for Spring and Summer 2020. For universities that will only be offering online classes for fall (such as many colleges and universities on the coasts), students will be required to leave the U.S. or transfer to another university which does not provide fully online instruction. Students at universities with a hybrid model, such as WSU, will be permitted to remain in the U.S. as long as our office certifies that each student is not enrolled entirely online and the student is taking the minimum number of online classes required to make progress toward their degree. To do this, we must reissue new I-20s to all of our international students and notate this information in the remarks area of the I-20. Students at universities offering hybrid classes (such as WSU) will not be allowed to maintain an active SEVIS record if they will remain outside of the U.S. for the Fall 2020 term. Instead, we must terminate the SEVIS record for Authorized Early Withdrawal. Students can still continue to enroll in as many online classes as they want at WSU – they will simply need a new I-20 when they return to the U.S. in a future term. Please note that in order to issue a new I-20, a new financial statement may be required. You may also have to pay the I-901 SEVIS fee again (currently $350) and your practical training eligibility may reset (meaning you will have to study for one full academic year before you can do CPT or OPT). We are still developing a system by which students will need to report to OIE their future plans. In the meantime, it is important that students who will remain in the U.S. for the Fall 2020 or, if currently abroad, return to the U.S. for Fall 2020, enroll in a full course of study that is not all online or hybrid without a physical presence component. Students who have no physical presence requirement for any of their Fall 2020 courses will be required to leave the U.S. We understand that students have many questions regarding their Fall plans and we are working diligently to develop an FAQ section that should be published on our website in the next few days. We appreciate your patience.

title: Spring 2022 FAQs for International Students
text: Spring 2022 FAQs for International Students - FAQs for Returning International Students Enrolling for Spring 2022 IMPORTANT: Return often for updates Last updated: January 3, 2022 FAQ 1: Why do I have a SEVIS hold on my account? All F-1 students have a SEVIS hold on their account. Before you can enroll for the Spring 2022 term, you will need to complete online SEVIS check-in to clear your SEVIS hold. The Spring 2022 check-in will be available beginning Monday, October 18. Check-ins received before 8 a.m. will be cleared the same business day. Check-ins received after 8 a.m. will be cleared the next business day. FAQ 2: Can I count more than one online class towards my full course of study requirement in Spring 2022? F-1 international students must follow traditional distance learning regulations for the Spring 2022 term onward. This is a change from Spring 2020, Fall 2020, Spring 2021, and Fall 2021 terms when the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) issued special COVID-19 provisions temporarily suspending the normal rule. Immigration regulations state that only one distance education course of up to three credit hours may count towards a student’s minimum full-time enrollment requirement each semester. Hours beyond the minimum enrollment requirement can be in any learning format. Please note that the definition of a distance learning course is one that does not require any physical class meetings or other in-person interaction throughout the semester; at WSU this would be any course with an online (IIS or IIE) instructional method. Hybrid courses have an in-person component so they do not count as distance learning. If you have any questions about enrollment requirements and the Spring 2022 term, please email iss@wichita.edu or call/visit during walk-in advising hours, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday afternoons from 1:00 to 4:00 p.m. FAQ 3: How do I find out the instruction method for a particular class? When searching the class schedule , select the course and click on the course title to see the instructional method. For example, You can also search for classes by type of instruction method if you use the advanced search feature: FAQ 4: I'm traveling outside of Kansas during the Winter Break. Do I have to quarantine when I return to Wichita? For current quarantine requirements, visit https://www.coronavirus.kdheks.gov/175/Travel-Exposure-Related-Isolation-Quaran . Please note that KDHE updates this information regularly so be sure to check it often. FAQ 5: Do I need a paper I-20 to re-enter the U.S.? The Student and Exchange Visitor Program announced in Fall 2021 that schools are permanently allowed to send Forms I-20s by email to students. However, students must print and sign Form I-20 and carry this paper document with them while traveling. FAQ 6: Is a COVID-19 vaccination required to enter the U.S.? Beginning November 8, 2021, nonimmigrants will be required to show proof of being fully vaccinated against COVID-19 in order to enter the U.S. More information about the vaccination requirement and limited exceptions is available at: https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/travelers/noncitizens-US-air-travel.html FAQ 7: Am I required to have a negative COVID-19 test to return to the U.S. even if I am fully vaccinated? All international travelers, regardless of vaccination status, are required to take a COVID-19 viral test no more than 24 hours before traveling by air to the U.S. For more information about testing requirements, please visit the CDC website. NOTE: This is a complex, challenging, and fluid situation which continues to evolve rapidly. All information on this page is subject to change as deemed necessary by University leadership in accordance with guidance and recommendations issued by federal, state, and local public health and government officials.

title: Student Ambassador Society
text: Student Ambassador Society - Student Ambassador Society (SAS) enhances the image of Wichita State University by participating in various outreach programs. As a service organization, SAS members work alongside the Office of Admissions to discuss the benefits of a university experience, especially at WSU, by sharing their experiences as WSU students. SAS also hosts student and non-student VIPs while they're on the WSU campus. Apply to SAS Leadership Conference Ask a Shocker About SAS Responsibilities Student ambassadors volunteer about 20-25 hours per semester. Twelve hours are dedicated to biweekly meetings and 8-12 hours are spent assisting and supporting the Office of Admissions . Ways that ambassadors help the Office of Admissions include but are not limited to: Working for the Office of the President and the WSU Foundation hosting dignitaries and donors Mingling with students and parents at on-campus programs Writing postcards and making phone calls to prospective students Serving on student panels during group visits and on-campus programs Attending Discover Wichita State programs with admissions staff Hosting an annual leadership conference for high school student leaders Providing a current student's perspective on WSU Benefits Impacting the future of the university by interacting with prospective students, current students, university faculty and staff, and alumni Giving back to the university Professional and social networking Service to the Wichita community Meeting fellow WSU students Leadership development Outreach to WSU campus and the Wichita community Enhancing your Wichita State collegiate experience History In the spring of 1995, students in Shocker Ambassadors and the Student Alumni Association united to become the WSU Student Ambassador Society (SAS) and work as volunteers alongside the Office of Admissions in recruitment efforts. Throughout its existence, the group has grown in size, but not changed in purpose. SAS has initiated many sustainable and successful activities including: the annual state-wide SAS Leadership Conference for high school students the endowed Amie Montgomery scholarship Gore Core, a celebration of the top students who compete in the Distinguished Scholarship Invitational Graduates of this group have gone on to be successful lawyers, doctors, educators, engineers, performers, health care practitioners and business professionals who maintain their dedication and loyalty to Wichita State and the Wichita community. The motto of the Student Ambassador Society is "Loyal service through Shocker spirit." This motto has been adopted as a lifetime commitment for its members. The group is currently advised by Quinn Munk and Sheelu Surender.

title: A Guide for Living on Campus
text: A Guide for Living on Campus - Moving In You don't need to bring your entire house (Oops, I learned this the hard way). Here are a few tips I learned: Make a detailed packing list of essentials before you move in Bring a few items that make your space feel like home! Here are a few items I enjoyed having: Coffee Maker: Super handy not only for coffee, but for hot water for mac and cheese, ramen, etc. Mini Air Fryer: Also nifty for midnight snacks. Over-The-Door Organizer: SUPER handy for extra storage in a dorm space. Mattress Topper (Twin XL): This makes those post-class naps hit different. Power Strip: You can never have too many outlets. Fan: Living with others, you never know what the temperature of the room will end up being. Microwave/Mini Fridge: What can I say? I like food. Sharing a Living Space Communication is key! Don't be afraid to express your concerns to your roommate(s), and at the same time, be open to hearing what they have to say to you. Here are some tips: Communication from the start about your expectations as a roommate will start you on the right foot to a successful living environment. Everyone is raised differently and likes their space to look different ways, so get to know your roommate and their preferences. Setting Rules and Boundaries Set rules and boundaries from the very beginning with your roommate(s) on things such as playing music, cleanliness, inviting guests over, sharing items, etc. Doing this from the beginning will make things much easier. Make sure to stick to these boundaries because as soon as you start to be lenient with them, they might become wishy-washy. Also, your roommate does not have to be your best friend. It is completely fine to spend time with your roommate(s) and get to know them, but at the same time it is also important to not spend all your time with them, as that can lead to some difficult situations. Don't be afraid to get out of the room and hang out with some other friends as well! title: Four Differences Between Dual Credit and Advanced Placement
text: Four Differences Between Dual Credit and Advanced Placement - There are a lot of questions out there about dual credit and advanced placement. This post will help clear up the four main differences between AP and dual credit and what students should consider. Who is offering the course Dual Credit: These are being offered by a college and are available to high school students, and are taught by university approved teachers AP: These are organized and taught by the high school How credit is awarded Dual Credit: Students are awarded college credit for passing the course. AP: Students take a standardized test at the end of the school year. If they meet the minimum score determined by the college they attend, they receive credit. Course length Dual Credit: These classes can last for one semester to one academic year – depending on the way it is laid out at the high school. Often they will be one semester long like a traditional college course. AP: Classes last a whole school year. Cost Dual Credit: Courses can be as little as $100 per course (like here at Wichita State) and go up to $100 per credit hour ($300 per course), or more. AP: Exams cost $96 per exam. In summary, dual credit options are an incredible way to obtain college credit at substantially discounted rates and potentially drastically reduce the time you spend in college. Want to learn more about dual credit opportunities at Wichita State? Reach out to us at concurrent@wichita.edu .
