title: Guía Para Padres a Wichita State
text: Guía Para Padres a Wichita State - QUERIDOS PADRES: ¡Saludos desde Wichita State University! Usted y su estudiante están a punto de embarcarse en un viaje importante. Ayudar a su estudiante a elegir la universidad adecuada es un proceso importante y, a menudo, abrumador. La información adjunta está diseñada para ayudarlos a trabajar juntos en la toma de esta decisión importante. Algunas cosas importantes que puede hacer mientras ayuda a su estudiante: anime a su estudiante a visitar las universidades que más le interesan; solicitar admisión y becas con anticipación; investigue cada opción; y hablar con estudiantes actuales de cada escuela. Estos pasos ayudarán a tomar la importante decisión de qué escuela se adapta mejor. Nos apasiona la solidez de nuestros programas académicos, las oportunidades incomparables para el aprendizaje basado en la experiencia y una vida universitaria próspera. Yo los animo a que programen una visita oficial al campus. Estoy seguro de que quedará impresionado con lo que ofrece WSU. Wichita State ha sido la opción educativa para líderes famosos, incluidos los cofundadores de Pizza Hut, Dan y Frank Carney, y Bill Parcels, entrenador en jefe de la NFL y ganador del Super Bowl. El cofundador de Garmin International, Gary Burrell, la meteoróloga jefe ganadora del premio Emmy, Lisa Teachman, y la estrella de ópera ganadora del premio Grammy, Joyce DiDonato, son todos graduados de Wichita State. Dado que nuestra universidad ha experimentado una inscripción récord en los últimos años, este es el mejor momento para ser un Shocker y unirse a los rangos de estos estimados exalumnos que comenzaron su futuro en Wichita State. Desde los recursos ilimitados de nuestro Campus de Innovación en rápido crecimiento hasta la investigación innovadora y las oportunidades de aprendizaje aplicado para estudiantes de todas las especialidades, es un día emocionante para ser un Shocker. Esperamos darle la bienvenida en el campus pronto para que puedan ver de primera mano todo lo que ofrecemos. Atentamente, Bobby Gandu Vicepresidente Adjunto de Gestión Estratégica de Inscripciones y Director de Admisiones Wichita State University EXPLORE EL FUTURO DE SU ESTUDIANTE Como la única universidad de investigación urbana de Kansas, Wichita State ofrece excelentes oportunidades académicas, una vibrante vida en el campus y un acceso incomparable a profesionales de la industria. Con una inscripción de 17,500, Wichita State se enorgullece de la atención especializada a cada estudiante, posible gracias a una proporción de estudiantes por docente de 20:1 y el hecho de que el 93% de nuestras clases tienen menos de 50 estudiantes. Los miembros respetados de la facultad se dedican a la enseñanza, la erudición, la investigación y el servicio público. Y con más de 300 clubes sociales y de intereses especiales, los estudiantes pueden encontrar su lugar dentro de nuestra diversa comunidad universitaria. VISITANDO EL CAMPUS Puede leer sobre escuelas, revisar sus sitios web y hablar con representantes de admisiones en las ferias universitarias, pero nada puede reemplazar la experiencia de visitar un campus universitario para ver por sí mismo sus instalaciones, hablar con estudiantes y profesores y visitar las residencias estudiantiles. En Wichita State, invitamos a usted y a su estudiante a venir al campus para ver la experiencia especial de ser un Shocker. Se encuentran disponibles visitas personalizadas al campus (con al menos dos semanas de antelación) y anualmente se ofrecen días de visitas para programas especiales. Para saber qué tipo de visita se adapta mejor a sus necesidades y horario, consulte wichita.edu/visit . Obtenga más información sobre las experiencias de Shockers viendo Shock Docs en wichita.edu/ShockDoc . Hacer la mejor elección universitaria requiere mucho trabajo. Estos son algunos de los hitos más importantes que debe celebrar a medida que su estudiante avanza en el proceso: Realizar el examen ACT o SAT Si su estudiante aún no ha tomado el examen ACT o SAT, anímelo a tomarlo al menos una vez durante su tercer año de la preparatoria y nuevamente a principios de su último año. Ser admitido para ser considerado para becas Anime a su estudiante a ser admitido a principios del otoño de su último año. Al hacerlo, su estudiante tendrá acceso a más oportunidades de becas y atención personalizada. En Wichita State, comenzamos a otorgar becas en septiembre del último año de la preparatoria. Para ser considerado para los concursos grandes de becas en WSU, presente su solicitud antes del 15 de octubre. wichita.edu/scholarships Hablar con un representante de admisiones Los representantes en la Oficina de Admisiones de Wichita State serán recursos valiosos para usted y su estudiante. Conéctese con el representante de la escuela preparatoria de su estudiante visitando wichita.edu/admissionsstaff . Visitar el campus Programe una visita oficial a Wichita State en wichita.edu/visit . Avísenos con al menos dos semanas de antelación para que podamos adaptar el día a sus necesidades. O si prefieren visitar desde la comodidad de su hogar, consulte nuestro recorrido virtual en wichita.edu/virtualtour . Solicitar ayuda financiera federal Solicite ayuda financiera federal antes de la fecha de prioridad de Wichita State durante el último año de la preparatoria de su estudiante para garantizar una consideración completa para todos los premios. Visite studentaid.gov para obtener más información. Discutir cómo se financiará la universisad Hable abiertamente con su estudiante sobre cuánto podría contribuir a su educación y cuánto necesitará financiar por su cuenta. Considere también el valor como parte de la ecuación. Wichita State está clasificada entre las 80 mejores universidades más asequibles según College Consensus, además de ser la universidad de investigación más asequible de Kansas. Nuestros estudiantes ganan anualmente más de $30 millones en pasantías y puestos de trabajo estudiantil en el campus, lo que ayuda a financiar sus propios gastos universitarios y al mismo tiempo adquiere experiencia profesional. Hacer un calendario y comenzar a investigar escuelas. Compile una lista de fechas límite de admisión, ayuda financiera y becas. Piense en lo que su estudiante está buscando en una universidad: especialidades, tamaño de las clases, oportunidades de pasantías, ubicación, costos y actividades. Recuérdeles que el lugar que elijan asistir será su hogar durante los próximos cuatro o cinco años, por lo que deben considerar seriamente los diversos aspectos de cada escuela. Manténgase actualizado con la universidad de interés de su estudiante Una vez que su estudiante seleccione una especialización, siga las redes sociales de ese colegio académico. Para Wichita State, le recomendamos consultar wichita.edu/blog . ADMISIONES Para ser admitidos en Wichita State University, los estudiantes que se gradúan de una escuela preparatoria acreditada, menor de 21 años, DEBEN : Tener un GPA (promedio) acumulativo no ponderado de 2.25 en una escala de 4.00, O Lograr una puntuación compuesta de ACT de 21 o mejor O una puntuación compuesta mínima de 1080 en el SAT (las pruebas son opcionales para admisión), Y , si corresponde, lograr un GPA de 2.0 en todos los créditos universitarios tomados en la escuela preparatoria NOTA: Residentes de Kansas de escuelas no acreditadas o escuelas en el hogar deben lograr un puntaje calificado de ACT o GED. No residentes de escuelas no acreditadas se consideran caso por caso. Consulte nuestro sitio web para obtener más información sobre los requisitos de admisión. El proceso de admisión requiere la presentación de una solicitud de admisión y una tarifa de solicitud de $40. Su estudiante deberá ingresar su GPA no ponderado en una escala de 4.0 y puntajes de exámenes en la aplicación. Visite wichita.edu/apply . REPRESENTANTES DE ADMISIONES Como un recurso valioso para usted y su estudiante, los representantes de admisiones están ahí para responder sus preguntas y ayudarlo a aprender más sobre una escuela. Aquí hay algunas preguntas que quizás desee hacer a los representantes de Wichita State: ¿Qué pueden ofrecerle a mi estudiante que otras escuelas no puedan? ¿Cuáles son las especialidades más sólidas que se ofrecen en WSU? ¿Cuáles son los beneficios educativos para que mi estudiante esté en la ciudad de Wichita? ¿Cómo obtendrá mi estudiante experiencia del mundo real antes de graduarse de la universidad? ¿Qué hacen los estudiantes para divertirse fuera del campus? ¿Qué recursos existen para facilitar el éxito académico de mi estudiante? Los representantes de admisiones de Wichita State se asignan según las escuelas preparatorias. Llámenos o visite wichita.edu/admissionsstaff para encontrar más información sobre su representante de admisiones. WICHITA STATE SCHOLARSHIPS En Wichita State, el GPA y la puntuación del examen que su estudiante envía en su solicitud de admisión es todo lo que necesita para ser considerado para nuestras Becas al Mérito de cuatro años para estudiantes de primer año. Por otra parte, las becas están disponibles únicamente según el GPA. También podrían calificar para algunos de los más de $105 millones en otras becas y ayuda financiera que WSU otorga cada año. Entre las becas disponibles en WSU se encuentran las otorgadas a través del Distinguished Scholarship Invitational (DSI), que incluye becas Harry Gore Memorial de $64,000, uno de los premios universitarios más grandes de Kansas. Cualquier estudiante de ultimo año de preparatoria que solicite admisión a WSU antes del 15 de octubre, tenga al menos un GPA no ponderado de 3.50 o haya obtenido una puntuación compuesta de 27 o más en el ACT (o SAT equivalente), o se encuentre en el 10% superior de su clase de último año es elegible para participar. Visite Ayuda Financiera y Becas para más detalles . APLICANDO PARA AYUDA FINANCIERA FEDERAL Complete la Solicitud Gratuita de Ayuda Federal para Estudiantes (FAFSA) pronto cuando se abra. Se anima a los estudiantes y padres a presentar la solicitud en línea en studentaid.gov . Los plazos varían dependiendo de la institución. Si se eligen para la verificación, es posible que los estudiantes deban presentar documentación adicional, incluidas copias de las transcripciones de las declaraciones de impuestos. Comuníquese con la Oficina de Ayuda Financiera para obtener más información. Estos documentos se le solicitarán sólo si su FAFSA se selecciona para verificación. Los prestatarios por primera vez en Wichita State deben completar un acuerdo de préstamo conocido como Loan Agreement for a Master Promissory Note (MPN) y hacer un asesoramiento sobre préstamos en línea. Ambos se pueden hacer en studentaid.gov . La Solicitud Gratuita de Ayuda Federal para Estudiantes (FAFSA) es el formulario que su estudiante presentará para ser considerado para recibir ayuda financiera, como becas, préstamos y trabajo y estudio. Se espera que su familia proporcione información sobre los ingresos del año pasado, los activos y el hogar como parte de la FAFSA. Se les anima a los estudiantes a presentar la FAFSA antes de la fecha límite de prioridad de Wichita Stte. Consulte el sitio web para obtener detalles y fechas específicas. Al presenter la FAFSA, los estudiantes deben incluir el código escolar federal de WSU, 001950 . Al hacerlo, se garantiza que los resultados de la FAFSA se enviarán a WSU. TIPOS DE AYUDA FINANCIERA Wichita State otorga varios tipos de ayuda financiera, que incluyen: Becas: Fondos que los estudiantes pueden solicitar o ganar a través de la excelencia académica y no es necesario reembolsarlos. Subsidio: Fondos basados en necesidades financieras que no necesitan ser reembolsados. Préstamos: Fondos con tasas de interés fijas y bajas que deben reembolsarse. Estudio y Trabajo: Fondos que los estudiantes obtienen a través del empleo en Wichita State. Para ser considerado para cualquiera de estos tipos de ayuda, los estudiantes deben completar la FAFSA y indicar que los resultados se envíen a Wichita State enumerando nuestro código escolar federal, 001950 . Debido a que algunos programas tienen fondos limitados, se anima a los estudiantes a presentar su solicitud con anticipación. TIPOS DE PROGRAMAS DE PRÉSTAMO Préstamos Directos Los préstamos directos representan la mayor parte de la ayuda federal para estudiantes. La cantidad anual que un estudiante puede pedir prestado está determinada por el nivel de grado del estudiante en la universidad. Hay dos tipos de Préstamos Directos: subsidiados (basados en la necesidad) y no subsidiados (no basados en la necesidad). Préstamos PLUS Federal Parent Loan (PLUS) permite a los padres con un buen historial de crédito obtener préstamos para cubrir los gastos educativos de cada hijo que sea un estudiante universitario dependiente registrado en clases al menos medio tiempo. Para obtener más información sobre el préstamo PLUS y el proceso de solicitud, vaya a wichita.edu/financialaid . PLANES DE PAGO OPCIONALES Un plan de pago a corto plazo está disponible para ayudar a los estudiantes a pagar la matrícula y las tarifas. El plan de pago requiere un pago inicial sobre la matrícula y las tarifas al momento de pagar la tarifa y el saldo se puede pagar a lo largo del semestre en tres pagos iguales (dos cuotas iguales para la sesión de verano). Hay un cargo administrative no reembolsable asociado con este plan. Para más información, visita wichita.edu/acctsrec . 10 CONSEJOS DE LOS PADRES DE ESTUIDANTES ACTUALTES DE WICHITA STATE Sepa que los estudiantes cambian de especialidad. Tenga cuidado al elegir una universidad para un programa específico. En su lugar, asegúrese de que el ajuste general sea bueno más allá de la especialidad. Hable con sus hijos sobre cómo interactuar con el personal del campus y sus profesores mientras están en la escuela secundaria. Estos son profesionales que pueden ser recursos, referencias y redes para el futuro de su estudiante. Si puede lograr que funcione financieramente, anímelos a vivir en el campus. Si puede proporcionar una estructura de incentivos, puede ayudar a que su estudiante tenga un mejor desempeño. Deje que sus alumnos fracasen con una red de seguridad. Tomar riesgos es parte de la universidad, pero ayúdelos a recoger algunas de las piezas cuando lo necesiten. Anímelos a participar en actividades estudiantiles, encontrar un trabajo en el campus y desafiarse avsí mismos para conocer gente nueva. Hoy en día, los empleadores y las universidades demandan habilidades interpersonales. Ayude a sus estudiantes entender que llegar a tiempo, ser amigable, hacer un esfuerzo adicional y hacer un seguimiento con las personas se destacan entre quienes toman decisiones. title: Student Accommodations and Testing | Parent Information Workshop
text: Student Accommodations and Testing | Parent Information Workshop - Office of Student Accommodations and Testing Providing accommodations, access and proctored testing services to Wichita State University students. Frequent questions I think I have a learning disability. Can OSAT evaluate me so I can receive accommodations? No, OSAT does not evaluate students for disabilities. Referrals to qualified professionals will be provided upon request for a student to pursue independently. Can OSAT assist me with getting accommodations in my residence hall? Yes. OSAT staff and Residence Life coordinate services to meet your needs. Is there a fee to take a proctored test? Yes. However, students registered with OSAT are exempt from paying the exam fee. Fees for exams can be found on our website. What type of documentation is needed to receive accommodations? IEP or 504 Plans Doctor's note Psychological / Educational Testing results Counselor / Therapist Letter For housing accommodations: Doctor, Counselor, or Therapist letter stating the direct need for housing accommodations and/or Emotional Support Animals We're here for you Wichita State University welcomes a diverse student body and the Office Student Accommodations and Testing (OSAT) is committed to promoting access and inclusion for all members of our campus community. The law states that a disability is a type of physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities. Examples include, but are not limited to, the following: Attention deficit / hyperactivity Autism spectrum Developmental Health / physical (acute and/or chronic) Deaf / hard of hearing Learning Mental health / psychological Mobility Neurological Speech / language Temporary conditions Vision All accommodations are provided free of charge to registered students, and are determined on a case-by-case basis, according to the nature of the disability and to meet each student's individual needs. The decision to self-identify is a personal one. Students with disabilities are welcome to discuss concerns with staff. Accommodation Types Instructional accommodations are changes to the delivery of classroom instruction or the accompanying materials. These accommodations change how students learn but do not change what they learn Instructional accommodation examples may include: Large print handouts Access to breaks Note Takers Testing accommodations are changes to the format of a test or its administration procedures. Testing accommodations change how students are tested but do not change what a test measures. Testing accommodation examples may include: Extended time Distraction-free environment Open notes/text Testing We offer a quiet, distraction-free space to take exams. We offer several types of exams for students and members of the surrounding community. A few of the most popular exams we offer include: Make-up Exams, including: Paper/Pencil, Online Accommodations Exams Exams for Credit, including: CLEP, DSST, Departmental Exams Certiﬁcation Exams Institutional Exams, including: I-TOEFL, I-ACT The Office of Student Accommodations and Testing is certified by the National College Testing Association (NCTA) and adheres to professional standards and guidelines. Apply for accommodations at wichita.edu/accommodations . Schedule an exam at www.registerblast.com/wsu . title: Counseling and Psychological Services | Parent Information Workshop
text: Counseling and Psychological Services | Parent Information Workshop - Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS) Therapy Services CAPS offers affordable individual, couples, and group therapy If a student is looking to begin services, they can schedule their first appointment online or by calling Services provided by licensed counselors or supervised by licensed counselors Crisis Services If a student is in a mental health crisis, CAPS offers a safe location and counselors who can assist during regular business hours Examples of a mental health crisis include: immediate thoughts of suicide/self harm, assault or abuse Students can also seek help via the Suicide Prevention Lifeline (988) and the Crisis Text Line (741-741) Common concerns we treat Anxiety (of all kinds) Depression Adjustment difficulty Relationship challenges Identity concerns Substance use/abuse Mood disorders Suicidal ideation And so many more! If you’re thinking individual therapy is the best modality, these are some of the common concerns we see at CAPS. It is quite rare for CAPS to refer you out to someone else. We are able to see and treat most folks who walk through our doors. If we think any of these challenges might be better managed with medication, we can talk about that together and help get you set up with a provider at Student Health. * * It is important to note that you do not need to come to an individual therapy appointment to gain medication services. If you already have medication or are confident in starting them without therapy, you are allowed to directly call and make a medication appt. with Student Health. Counseling and Psychological Services One of the beautiful things about all aspects of health being under one roof means that it’s usually a one stop shop. So you can receive both physical, mental, and medication services at the SWC. Note: We only see enrolled students. title: Student Engagement and Belonging | Parent Information Workshop
text: Student Engagement and Belonging | Parent Information Workshop - Student Engagement and Belonging Student Engagement & Belonging at Wichita State brings together key areas that support student connection and involvement, including leadership development, campus traditions, student organizations, and cultural experiences. Through programs, events, and support services, our goal is to help students find their place, build community, and make the most of their Shocker experience, in AND out of the classroom. As a department, our staff is committed to providing opportunities for students to actively engage in out-of-classroom experiences, heighten their sense of belonging through community, expand their professional network, and develop essential skills that will prepare them for whatever the future may bring. ShockerSync This is a great place to start your involvement journey and begin your community building experience. These student led groups span a wide variety of interests and can be categorized by academics, cultural, honor societies, special interests, religion, politics, sport clubs, and more. All our student organizations are hosted on an online portal called ShockerSync. ShockerSync allows you to search for organizations, find events and track your involvement. There are hundreds of ways to get engaged at Wichita State, and it can be overwhelming. If you can’t find your fit, we can help! Our staff will meet with you one-on-one and provide recommendations based on your interests, schedule and availability. If you don’t see an organization that represents you or your interests – you can always start your own. Download your event pass Add your event pass to your wallet By creating an account in ShockerSync, there is now an option to add your event pass to your Apple or Google wallet. This allows you to quickly check-in to events happening on campus. NXT LVL Garage Party Greek Carnival Involvement & Community Fair Yard Show Big Bingo Wu's Big Event Shocktoberfest Traditions and Annual Events NXT LVL Garage Party Involvement & Community Fair Shockers After Dark Shocktoberfest & Family Weekend Student Activities Council (SAC) Student Activities Council coordinates 30-50 events and activities both on and off campus. Event highlights include BIG BINGO, Glow Dance Party, Shocktoberfest Spirit Competition, and De-Stress Fest. These experiences are coordinated by students like you and members can elect to serve on one of their five planning committees. Student Belonging Coalition (SBC) This group focuses on cultural programming and our heritage month celebrations—so things like Black History Month, Hispanic Heritage Month, APIDA events, and more. It’s all about helping students see themselves represented and celebrated, and creating a space where everyone can find community. Leadership Programs There are many leadership programs available to help you develop your skills. Through series programs, conferences, events and learning tools, students can choose how they would like to learn about leadership. Immersive Leadership Institute A four-day experience for new Shockers looking to get a head start on their campus engagement experiences. Participants earn college credit for attending. $75 fee covers entire cost of course enrollment. Apply today at wichita.edu/ILI. Applications due August 1. Shocker Strengths This program empowers students by connecting them with their unique CliftonStrengths! It aims to foster a deeper understanding of their innate talents and guides them toward academic, personal, and professional success. Fraternity & Sorority Life Fraternity and Sorority life at Wichita State University is full of tradition, brotherhood/sisterhood, and pride. This community gives you the opportunity to develop leadership skills, give back through philanthropy and meet new friends who share similar interests and values. We currently have 26 fraternities and sororities that have a variety of backgrounds, values, and missions. We recommend doing your research and getting to know the chapters to know what the best fit is for you. 7 IFC fraternities • 6 CGC fraternities & sororities • 8 NPHC fraternities & sororities • 5 PC sororities Interfraternity Council: Recruit year-round Cultural Greek Council: Recruit as needed National Pan-Hellenic Council: Recruit as needed Panhellenic Council: Formal recruitment process. The deadline is August 20 Community Service Board Community Service Board is a student organization that works to address issues of public concern through service in the community. CSB brings students together to develop service events that will create a positive impact in our community. This is a great way to give back to the community with your friends. Many of you will likely need to complete community service hours at some point during your college career; whether it’s for a class, scholarship or organization. Community Service Board is a great way to complete those hours. Areas of focus Food & Hunger Health Poverty & Homelessness Sustainability Youth & Education VolunteerICT There are many opportunities for service within the Wichita community. We host all those opportunities on VolunteerICT. VolunteerICT provides you with service opportunities based on your interests, specific agencies and location. Student Government Association Wichita State Student Government Association is governed by students and committed to student issues and concerns. Student Government Association empowers students to voice their opinions through campus committees and bi-weekly public senate meetings. SGA allocates over $10 million of annual student fees. SGA officers and agency members regularly meet with President Muma, Vice President & Provost Lounsbery, and other administrators including Vice Presidents and Deans. Shocker Support Locker Shocker Support Locker provides food, clothing, toiletries and baby/family products to students, faculty and staff at Wichita State. Students can take up to 10 items per week. Food for Fines is an initiative to support the Shocker Support Locker, while providing a cheaper opportunity to pay parking citations. Any person with a current WSU ID can donate a 7-14 food or hygiene items depending on the price of the citation. Food for Fines donation periods occur at various times throughout the academic year. Agencies Additionally – our department also supports eight student-led agencies that serve specific student populations and interest areas. These agencies plan events, provide support, and build community for students from a variety of backgrounds and identities. They also help amplify student voices and make sure our campus is welcoming for everyone. The agencies include: Asian Student Conference Black Student Union First Generation Student Organization Graduate Student Council Hispanic American Leadership Organization International Student Union Shockers Vote Coalition Spectrum: LGBTQ & Allies Passage 2 Success Week-long retreat for incoming freshmen from diverse backgrounds to help in their transition to Wichita State University! The purpose of this retreat is to connect with other incoming students, meet current student leaders, explore Wichita and gain the skills and tools to be socially and academically successful. PASS This program is designed to help students not just stay in school, but truly thrive. It focuses on academic success , personal development , and on-time graduation by providing a range of support services. Through PASS, students have access to academic resources, cultural and educational events, and most importantly — mentorship and relationship-building with staff and peers who are invested in their success. It’s a great way to make a big campus feel smaller and ensure students feel seen, supported, and connected throughout their college journey. Bi-weekly workshops Time management Study skills Financial readiness Mental health Alternate Breaks Alternative Breaks is a week-long service-learning trip dedicated to immersing students in work on a social justice issue such as poverty, hunger and homelessness, access to education, shelter, environmental stewardship and more. Students learn the facts associated with these issues, what they can do to help, and how to become better leaders in their communities. Some locations in the past include Washington, D.C., Catalina Island, New York City and New Orleans. National Student Exchange If you’re looking to leave Kansas, the National Student Exchange is the perfect opportunity for you. National Student Exchange allows you to study at a domestic university for up to a full academic year while paying Wichita State tuition. There are nearly 200 universities within this program and includes the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam, Virgin Islands and Canada. Past participants have attended: University of Hawai’i at Mānoa University of the Virgin Islands St. Croix Montclair State University Northern Arizona University Student Engagement & Belonging Statistics show that students that are engaged on campus are more likely to stay at Wichita State and graduate. These opportunities help you to build a network of friends and professionals for your future career goals. Involvement allows you the opportunity to attend conferences and workshops that will help you gain new skills. And of course, it’s important to have fun and make memories. title: Early High School Graduates
text: Early High School Graduates - Learn more about the differences between early high school graduates and high school guest students at Wichita State. What's the difference between between a high school guest and an early high school graduate? Early high school graduates If you are a high school student who qualifies to graduate from high school early, fewer than four full years of high school, you may be eligible for admission to Wichita State University as a degree-bound student or take classes as a high school guest. Nondegree high school guest The high school guest program offers a special opportunity for academically talented high school students to take college courses at WSU before high school graduation and earn full college credit. Will I get scholarships and financial aid? Only early high school graduates can receive scholarships and financial aid. Students who qualify and receive a Freshman Merit Scholarship, or any other freshman scholarship offers, will receive their award starting in the fall semester, not mid-year spring semester. However, students who receive financial aid through the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) can apply that at the start of the spring semester. You can find more on scholarships at wichita.edu/scholarships . You can fill out the FAFSA at fafsa.gov . High school guests High school guests do not qualify for scholarships and financial aid. The High School Guest program is for nondegree students who are still planning on graduating in May. What paperwork do I need? Early high school graduates You must have a date of graduation prior to the start of your intended term of entry. If your high school transcript does not include an expected graduation date, we will allow a written letter from your high school stating your early graduation date. Example: If you graduate from high school in December, your transcript must indicate that you are graduating in December in order to start as a degree-bound student for the spring semester. If your high school does not produce a transcript with your graduation in December, we will accept a written letter from your high school. If your high school does not produce a transcript or letter with your intended graduation, you may take classes as a high school guest – see below. When you apply, your transcript must reflect that you have completed at least six semesters of high school work completed. Your counseling office must submit a signed Midterm Graduate / Early Release Form to our admissions office: admissions.processing@wichita.edu . Degree-bound admission requirements Applicants must meet full admission requirements to Wichita State University: Have a cumulative 2.25 or higher GPA on a 4.00 scale OR Achieve an ACT composite of 21 or higher OR a minimum combined SAT ERW+M score of 1080 (test optional for admission) Apply to be an early graduate degree-bound student High school guests All students entering Wichita State for the first time must submit: A nondegree high school guest application for admission A nonrefundable $25 application fee Official high school transcript, including the semester completed prior to the semester of guest enrollment. Nondegree high school guest admission requirements Completion of their sophomore year of high school and Have at least a 3.00 high school cumulative GPA High School Guests may take up to six credit hours each semester. Application deadlines for High School Guests: Spring Deadline: Jan. 15 Summer Deadline: May 15 Fall Deadline: Aug. 14 Apply to be a high school guest student What is the enrollment process? Early high school graduates Step 1 Set up your myWSU password. In order to sign up for orientation, enroll in classes and access your WSU email account, you will need to complete this two-step process. First, go to mywsu.wichita.edu and click on "Manage your password" in the upper-right corner. After setting up your password, log in to you myWSU account and click on "Manage your password" in the upper-left corner of your home tab to set up your security and OneStop questions. Step 2 Sign up to attend Orientation. Early High School Graduates will select a New Shocker Orientation date using their myWSU ID and password. New students will complete their New Shocker Orientation requirement through online modules. RSVP to begin your new student transition process. Once you've completed the RSVP, you'll have access to complete the Online Orientation Modules. Students can sign up for orientation at: wichita.edu/orientation Step 3 Schedule your advising appointment with First-Year Advising. As part of OneStop Student Services, First-Year Advising offers a holistic advising experience to assist students in their transition to college. Students entering WSU directly from high school are provided with all-in-one support in the areas of: building a semester schedule, setting up a degree plan, reviewing financial aid, understanding your bill and setting up payment plans. Our advisors also assist with admissions, academic advising, financial aid, registration and student accounts. Schedule your advising appointment at 316-978-7440, email onestop@wichita.edu or visit the OneStop website . Step 4 Attend Orientation. In order to confirm your enrollment and save your place in the incoming class, you're required to attend the Orientation that you signed up for. Step 5 Start classes! Spring 2021 classes will start on Feb. 1! High school guests High school guests do not go through New Shocker Orientation. Instead, high school guests work with the LAS Advising Center to get enrolled in classes for spring 2021. Contact them at 316-978-3700, option 2, or email las.advisor@wichita.edu .

title: Admisiones de Pregrado
text: Admisiones de Pregrado - ¡Bienvenidos a Wichita State! Si está listo para construir su futuro ideal, Wichita State es el lugar para hacerlo. Al combinar un ambiente universitario tradicional con los recursos, oportunidades y experiencias que se encuentran en la ciudad más grande de Kansas, WSU tiene todo lo que necesitas para tener éxito en la universidad y más allá. Para ayudarlo a usted y a su estudiante a navegar el proceso de admisión a la universidad, juntamos una selección de recursos de nuestro sitio en inglés y los traducimos en español. Si tiene alguna pregunta, no dude en comunicarse con cualquiera de nuestro personal universitario que habla español para obtener más información . Para su conveniencia, proporcionamos información importante sobre admisiones en español. En algunos casos, hemos incluido enlaces a partes en inglés del sitio web de Wichita State. Para ayudarle a traducir esa información, le recomendamos usar Chrome con la extensión Google Translate agregada. Aquí hay instrucciones sobre cómo agregar esa extensión . OneStop: ¿Cómo podemos ayudarle? ¡OneStop es un gran recurso para todos los estudiantes de WSU! ¡Podemos ayudarle con preguntas sobre cualquier cosa, desde admisiones, cuentas de estudiantes, ayuda financiera, registro y más! Eventos Para Hispanohablantes Visitas al Campus Preguntas Frecuentes ¿Cómo aplico a WSU? Aprenda sobre cómo aplicar a WSU ¿Cuándo debo aplicar? Wichita State tiene una política de admisiones continuas para todos los estudiantes que ingresan ( excepto los estudiantes invitados de la escuela preparatoria ), lo que significa que las aplicaciones se procesan a medida que se reciben. Los estudiantes deben aplicar con anticipación, antes del semestre en el que desean comenzar a tomar clases. Los estudiantes deben ser admitidos por completo como estudiantes con una especialidad declarara para recibir ayuda financiera, invitaciones a los competencias de becas de WSU o para ser considerados para las becas basadas en el mérito. Se aceptan solicitudes para los semestres de otoño, primavera y verano. Los estudiantes deben esperar recibir una decisión de WSU dentro de las dos semanas después de que la Oficina de Admisiones reciba todos los materiales de solicitud necesarios, incluidas las transcripciones y los puntajes de ACT / SAT. Soy un ex alumno invitado de la escuela preparatoria ¿Necesito volver a aplicar? Si estaba inscrito en WSU y en la escuela preparatoria al mismo tiempo, es probable que NO necesite volver a solicitar la admisión, sino que tendrá que actualizar a un estado con una especialidad declarara con nosotros. Necesitaremos las transcripciones oficiales de cualquier universidad a la que haya asistido anteriormente, para que podamos actualizar su archivo. Comuníquese con la Oficina de Admisiones al 316-978-3085 o visite el Marcus Welcome Center para analizar su situación específica con nuestro personal. ¿Cuáles son los requisitos básicos para ser admitido? Wichita State University sigue los criterios de admisión calificada (QA), establecidos por la Junta de Regentes de Kansas, al admitir los siguientes tipos de estudiantes de pregrado: Estudiantes entrantes de primer año Estudiantes transferidos Estudiantes adultos Estudiantes de educación en el hogar Estudiantes sin título, incluyendo invitados de la preparatoria y universitarios Estudiantes de inscripción concurrente Ex alumnos de WSU Personas mayores Requisitos de Admisión ¿A quién puedo contactar sobre el estado de mi solicitud? Los estudiantes pueden comunicarse con la Oficina de Admisiones de WSU para revisar el estado de una solicitud de admisión. Para comunicarse con admisiones, llame al 316-978-3085. Los estudiantes deben comunicarse con la Oficina de Ayuda Financiera para consultar el estado de su solicitud de ayuda financiera o el estado de otorgamiento de becas. Para comunicarse con Ayuda Financiera, llame al 316-978-3430 o visite visite el sitio web de Ayuda Financiera . ¿Cómo acepta WSU las transcripciones y los puntajes de las pruebas? ¿Puedo llevarlos a mano? WSU acepta transcripciones y puntajes de exámenes (ACT, SAT) en una variedad de formas. Algunos artículos se pueden llevar a mano, pero se aplican ciertas reglas y restricciones. Ver más información sobre el envío de transcripciones ¿Cómo cambio la información de mi solicitud o el semestre de asistencia? Si desea cambiar la información en su solicitud o actualizar su semestre de asistencia y ha presentado su solicitud a WSU dentro del año académico actual, puede actualizar su información en línea en wichita.edu/update o comunicarse con la Oficina de Admisiones directamente al 316-978- 3085. Si presentó su solicitud fuera del año académico actual, deberá volver a presentar su solicitud en la universidad. Si no está seguro de cuándo fue admitido, comuníquese con la Oficina de Admisiones al 316-978-3085. ¿Hay una forma que se necesita para los que se gradúan a mitad de período o temprano de la escuela preparatoria? Sí. Los graduados intermedios o tempranos de la escuela preparatoria deben completar una forma antes de asistir a Wichita State. title: Aplicar a WSU
text: Aplicar a WSU - Los estudiantes deben seguir estos pasos para aplicar a WSU: Estudiantes De Primer Año Aplique en cualquier momento después de su tercer año de escuela preparatoria. Los estudiantes de primer año que ingresan deben postularse temprano para recibir una consideración completa para el Programa de Becas de Mérito para estudiantes de primer año. No se requiere una solicitud de beca adicional. Los estudiantes solo necesitan ser admitidos completamente con los siguientes elementos en el archivo: Aplicación completa en papel o en línea Transcripciones oficiales de la escuela preparatoria enviadas directamente a WSU Puntuaciones ACT o SAT enviadas directamente a WSU Tarifa de solicitud no reembolsable de $40 Common App Wichita State es miembro de Common App . Si desea presentar una solicitud utilizando la aplicación común, agréguenos a su lista ‘My Colleges.’ Estudiantes de Primer Año: Requisitos de Admisión A los estudiantes de primer año se les asegura la admisión a Wichita State si cumplen con lo siguiente: 1.Promedio (GPA) acumulotivo de 2.25 o más alto (en una escala de 4.00) O 2. 21 en el ACT O 1060 en el SAT (prueba opcional para admisiones) Y , si es aplicable, lograr un GPA de 2.0 en todos los créditos univeresitarios obtenidos en la escuela secundaria. Por favor, tenga en cuenta que si no cumple con los requisitos de admisión garantizada, aún se le anima a postularse. Su solicitud será revisada de manera individual. Si se graduó de una escuela secundaria no acreditada o fue educado en casa debe: Lograr un 21 en el ACT o más alto O un 1060 en el SAT Y tener un GPA acumulotivo de 2.25 o más alto (en una escala de 4.00). Si se matricula en cursos universitarios mientras está en la escuela secundaria, también debe obtener un GPA de 2.00 o más alto en esos cursos. Si obtuvo su GED, debe: Para los exámanes de GED desde 2014 en adelante: tener una puntuación mínima de 150 en cada sub prueba, y una puntuación total de 680 para ser admitido. Para los exámenes de GED de 2002 a 2013: tener una puntuación mínima de 510 en cada sub prueba, y una puntuación total de 2550 para ser admitido. Estudiantes Transferidos Aplique al menos un semestre antes de transferirse a WSU. Las transferencias entrantes deben aplicar con anticipación, a fin de recibir una consideración completa para el Programa de Becas por Mérito de Transferencia. title: Ayuda Financiera y Becas
text: Ayuda Financiera y Becas - Ayuda Financiera La universidad puede ser una de las mayores y mejores inversiones de su vida, por lo que cuando se trata de pagar su educación, tiene opciones y estamos aquí para ayudarlo. Cada año, la Oficina de Ayuda Financiera desembolsa más de $100 millones en subvenciones, becas, estudio y trabajo y préstamos estudiantiles. La Oficina de Ayuda Financiera también puede responder preguntas y ofrecer orientación a través del proceso de encontrar soluciones efectivas para financiar su educación. Becas Financiar su educación de alta calidad en Wichita State es fácil. Simplemente obtenga la admisión y, si es elegible, le enviaremos una oferta de beca automática. También podría calificar para algunos de los más de $100 millones en otras becas y ayuda financiera que otorgamos cada año, incluidas las otorgadas a través de competencias de becas. Además, muchos de nuestros estudiantes de fuera del estado califican para la matrícula estatal o reducida. Fechas limites importantes Fecha límite de solicitud de competencias de becas: 10 de noviembre Fecha de prioridad para estudiantes de último año de preparatoria: 1 de diciembre Fecha de prioridad de estudiantes de transferencia: 1 de febrero Solicitud Gratuita de Ayuda Federal para Estudiantes (FAFSA) disponible: octubre Fecha de prioridad de FAFSA de Wichita State: 1 de abril Ayuda Financiera Solicitud de la Solicitud Gratuita de Ayuda Federal para Estudiantes (FAFSA) ¿Qué es la FAFSA? La FAFSA es la Solicitud Gratuita de Ayuda Federal para Estudiantes. Es el formulario que usa el gobierno federal para determinar su elegibilidad para recibir ayuda federal. Esta ayuda puede incluir subvenciones, becas, trabajo-estudio y préstamos. ¿Por qué debo completar la FAFSA? Completar la FAFSA le permite ser considerado para recibir ayuda financiera federal, estatal y algunos tipos de ayuda financiera institucional. La forma más rápida de enviar su FAFSA es en línea en studentaid.gov . Ambos métodos permiten que el procesador federal haga una "verificación final" de su información para asegurarse de que su FAFSA esté lista para ser procesada antes de enviarla. ¿Cuándo debo completar la FAFSA? ¿Hay una fecha límite? Termina tu FAFSA lo antes posible. El 1 de abril es la fecha de prioridad de WSU. Los estudiantes pueden presentar su solicitud después de esta fecha, pero la oportunidad de recibir algunos tipos de programas de ayuda se reducirá considerablemente. La elegibilidad para la Beca Federal Pell y/o los Préstamos Federales Directos no se ven afectados por esta fecha límite de prioridad. Debe completar la FAFSA cada año que desee ser considerado para recibir ayuda financiera. Revise toda su información cada año porque su elegibilidad puede cambiar según las circunstancias de su familia. ¿Cuál es el código escolar de Wichita State para la FAFSA? 001950 Oportunidades de Becas Becas al Mérito Simplemente obtenga la admisión y, si es elegible, le enviaremos su oferta de beca dentro de dos semanas. Sin formularios agotadores, sin esperas angustiosas, solo el prestigio de ser nombrado becario Shocker. Las oportunidades de becas al mérito están disponibles para estudiantes de primer año, transferidos, estudiantes del Colegio de Honores, finalistas por mérito nacional. Para obtener más información, visite wichita.edu/scholarships . Matrícula Estatal o Reducida Los estudiantes de Arkansas, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Dakota del Norte, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas y Wisconsin pueden calificar para la matrícula estatal o reducida. Para obtener más información, visite wichita.edu/tuitiondiscounts . Más formas de financiar su éxito Los estudiantes de WSU tienen acceso a millones en becas específicas para universidades y otras formas de ayuda financiera. Presente su Solicitud Gratuita de Ayuda Federal para Estudiantes (FAFSA) antes de la fecha límite prioritaria de WSU del 1 de abril. Para obtener más información, visite wichita.edu/financialaid . Becas de Colegio Académico Los colegios académicos de Wichita State otorgan anualmente más de $4.2 millones en becas disponibles, y la mayor parte del apoyo de becas para estudiantes actuales/continuos se proporciona a través de los colegios académicos. Para ser considerado para estos premios, los estudiantes deben solicitar estas becas cada año (generalmente a fines del otoño) a través de su colegio académico. Cada colegio tiene su propio proceso de solicitud y fecha límite. Visite la página web del colegio para obtener información e instrucciones para la solicitud. Las preguntas deben dirigirse al coordinador de becas de su colegio. Para obtener más información, visite wichita.edu/collegescholarships . Competencias de Becas Todas las Especialidades - Distinguished Scholarship Invitational Monto del premio: Hasta $64,000 El Distinguished Scholarship Invitational es una de las competencias de becas más destacadas del área, incluidas tres becas Harry Gore Memorial de $64,000, tres de las becas anuales de pregrado más grandes de Kansas. DSI se llevará a cabo en el campus el sábado 23 de noviembre. Los estudiantes deben estar presentes para participar. Si tiene alguna pregunta, comuníquese con la Oficina de Admisiones al 316-978-3085 o envíenos un correo electrónico a dsi@wichita.edu . Para ser elegible para competir, debe: Ser un estudiante en su último año de la escuela preparatoria Envíe los materiales de solicitud a Wichita State Cumplir con uno de los siguientes criterios: Tener un GPA mínimo no ponderado de 3.5, o Tener un puntaje compuesto mínimo de ACT de 27, o Tener un SAT compuesto mínimo de 1260, o Clasificarse en el top 10 por ciento de su clase al final de su tercer año Fechas Importantes de la beca Gore Fecha límite para materiales de la aplicación de WSU: 1 de noviembre de 2025 Fecha límite para materiales de becas: 10 de noviembre de 2025 Competencia: 22 de noviembre de 2025 Solicitar la Beca Distinguida por Invitación Obtenga más información sobre el Distinguished Scholarship Invitational (DSI) En 1952, Theodore y Ralph Gore establecieron la beca Harry Gore en memoria de su padre, Harry Gore, un inmigrante ruso que le dio una alta prioridad a la educación. Esta beca extraordinaria se ha otorgado anualmente desde 1954 a los estudiantes de primer año que ingresan a WSU que muestran un potencial sobresaliente para el liderazgo . Se ha convertido en uno de los premios más prestigiosos y codiciados en los Estados Unidos y fomenta el crecimiento personal y la participación en puestos de liderazgo. A través del proceso de DSI, tres estudiantes finalmente recibirán $64,000 para asistir a Wichita State University en el otoño. Los becarios Gore están muy involucrados en las actividades de los estudiantes y son líderes en todo el campus de Wichita State. No hay un tipo de persona que tenga éxito siendo un becario Gore. Cada uno es único y puede expresar sus opiniones a través de las actividades que realiza en el campus. Solicitud Además de las actividades grupales, presentarás la solicitud del concurso de becas. Tóme su tiempo en esto: ¡es la otra mitad de su puntaje en la competencia DSI! Algunos consejos mientras piense en la aplicación: Escriba sus ensayos en Word y transfiéralos a la aplicación. Pídele a alguien que revise tus ensayos varias veces. ¡Presume de ti mismo! Si vas a presumir, una solicitud de beca es el lugar para hacerlo. Dia de la competencia Si elige participar, puede esperar participar en las actividades a continuación el día de la competencia. ¡Estas actividades constituyen la mitad de su puntaje para la competencia DSI! La Creación de Consenso En esta sesión, a su grupo se le dará un escenario y se le pedirá que resuelva el problema. Los observadores observarán cómo su grupo interactúa entre sí. Cosas para pensar: ¿Estás escuchando las ideas de los demás? ¿Está usted participando en la discusión? Entrevista de Grupo En esta sesión, los observadores le harán una pregunta a cada estudiante de su grupo. Las preguntas se basan en opiniones, por lo que no hay respuestas correctas o incorrectas. Cosas para pensar: ¿Estás respondiendo la pregunta con confianza y mostrando tu personalidad? ¿Estás haciendo un buen contacto visual? ¿Está respondiendo de manera concisa? Secuencia de los eventos Noviembre: las solicitudes se revisan y califican. 22 de noviembre: día de la competencia DSI en el campus. Antes del 5 de diciembre: los estudiantes recibirán una notificación sobre cómo avanzar como semifinalistas de DSI. 16 de diciembre: Gore Core: un evento de celebración para los semifinalistas de DSI (no es obligatorio asistir) Para el 19 de diciembre: los semifinalistas recibirán una notificación sobre cómo avanzar como finalistas de DSI. 22 de enero: los finalistas de DSI participarán en una entrevista final con el comité de selección de Gore. 30 de enero: anuncio de los Becarios Gore 2025 Carreras de Negocios - Concurso de Beca Allen, Gibbs, y Houlik L.C. title: Amazon Career Choice
text: Amazon Career Choice - About the program Wichita State University serves as a partner school in Amazon's Career Choice program. The program offers annual tuition and textbook assistance for eligible associates that can be redeemed at Wichita State University – paying for up to $5,250 for full-time employees and $2,625 for part-time employees. This tuition voucher applies to any undergraduate program or credential, including degrees and certificates. Getting started Contact us Donisha Hoffine Director , Shocker Transfer Accelerator 316-978-7667 donisha.hoffine@wichita.edu Apply Online application Admission requirements Learn more Amazon website WSU Admissions website Frequently Asked Questions Am I eligible for the program? title: About the Gore Scholarship
text: About the Gore Scholarship - The Harry Gore Memorial Scholarship Program is designed to honor the legacy of Harry Gore, a distinguished community leader and advocate for education. The scholarship is awarded annually to high school seniors who have demonstrated outstanding academic achievement, community involvement, and a commitment to making a positive impact in their community. To be eligible for the Harry Gore Memorial Scholarship, applicants must be graduating seniors from a high school in the designated community, with a minimum GPA of 3.00. In addition to academic achievement, applicants must have a proven track record of community involvement and volunteerism. The Wichita State University scholarship committee looks for applicants who have made a significant impact on their community through volunteer work, leadership, and service. Recipients of the Harry Gore Memorial Scholarship receive financial support to help them pursue their educational goals at Wichita State University. In addition, recipients become part of a community of Gore Scholars who are dedicated to making a difference in their communities. Beyond the financial support, recipients of the Harry Gore Memorial Scholarship are also encouraged to become involved in community service and leadership activities during their time in college. Through the scholarship program, recipients have access to a network of alumni and mentors at Wichita State University who can provide guidance and support as they pursue their educational and career goals. The Harry Gore Memorial Scholarship program is a testament to the power of community involvement and the impact that one individual can have on the lives of many. Through this scholarship program, we hope to inspire future generations of community leaders who will continue to make a positive impact in their communities and beyond. Distinguished Scholarship Invitational The Distinguished Scholarship Invitational (DSI) is one of the area's most prominent scholarship competitions. Through the DSI process, three students will ultimately be awarded with $64,000 to attend Wichita State University in the fall. Gore Scholars are highly involved in student activities and are leaders across the Wichita State campus. There is not one type of person who makes a successful Gore Scholar. Each is unique and able to express their opinions through activities they pursue on campus. Eligible students apply to compete. On competition day, students participate in consensus-building activities and a group interview. Learn more about scholarship competitions at Wichita State Gore Scholars home

title: Arrival Information
text: Arrival Information - When you arrive on campus All University offices are open Monday - Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Offices are closed on Saturdays and Sundays. If you did not present official final transcripts and degree certification when you applied for admission, please bring your official final transcripts and degree certificate with you to Wichita. These need to be provided to the Graduate School so your admission can be finalized. This should be done by the end of the first week of classes. What you uploaded in your application portal is not considered official. Check-in You will receive further email communication from the Office of International Education on how to schedule your check-in time approximately one month before the start of classes. You will not be allowed to enroll without completing the check-in process. Accommodations Graduate students may choose to live on campus in one of our apartment style residence halls: The Flats and The Suites. Information on these on-campus housing opportunities can be found at wichita.edu/housing . Most graduate students prefer to live off campus. While the University cannot assist in finding these locations, International Education does provide information that can assist in locating housing within walking distance to the WSU campus. In addition to paying rent, students living off campus should also expect to pay for utilities (electric, water, gas), as well as internet and cable television, if desired). Expenses are estimated on the I-20 cost of attendance and may vary significantly, depending on where you chose to live. Remember that housing costs on the I-20 are only estimated for 9 months. Students staying in the U.S. all year should expect to contribute more to their cost of living expenses. New students should not expect the University to have housing available upon arrival to Wichita. Many incoming students find the need to reserve a hotel room for a few days while coordinating housing upon arrival. Additionally, students may connect with international student organizations through social media to find accommodations. Apartment hunting? The Wichita Apartment Guide is available online at apartmentguide.com . The university is happy to provide a centralized place to start your search for an off-campus apartment or house. Please visit https://offcampushousing.wichita.edu/listing . Health matters Insurance Wichita State University requires that all international students have medical insurance. The cost of medical care in the U.S. is very expensive so we want to make sure that you are covered by insurance in the event of illness, pregnancy, or serious injury. You will be automatically charged for medical insurance unless you can provide proof of medical insurance coverage from another provider that meets U.S. Affordable Care Act benefit requirements. For more details, please visit wichita.edu/MedicalInsurance Vaccination records Please bring your vaccination records with you to the U.S. If you need any vaccinations when you arrive, your student health insurance will cover them and you can get them at Student Health. We recommend that you take care of any existing medical or dental problems at home since student medical insurance does not cover routine dental work or eye examinations. TB Testing All new students are required to complete state-mandated TB testing prior to enrollment. All appointments are scheduled online by following the instructions on the provided link. University health insurance begins on August 1. Any services you receive prior to this date are not covered by insurance. If you plan on scheduling your tuberculosis test prior to this date you will need to pay the $80 fee at the time of the appointment. Scheduling Instructions: TB Testing Location (Google Maps): https://g.page/SteveClarkYMCA?share Opening a bank account After arriving in Wichita, you may open a bank account. We have popular banks nearby - Meritrust Credit Union at Braeburn Square on campus, and Bank of America has a branch next to our campus. All these banks have an ATM located in the Rhatigan Student Center. In order to open an account, you will need to show the bank your passport, your I-20, and proof of your address in Wichita (such as your housing contract or apartment rental contract). You will receive an ATM card after opening an account so you can get cash quickly and easily. Orientation We are excited you have chosen to attend WSU and we are here to support you. There's a lot to love about being a part of Shocker Nation and it's our mission to guide you in transitioning to life as a WSU student. New graduate student orientation is being held virtually. As a new graduate student, you will need to complete the online orientation. You will receive emails with directions prior to the start of the semester. The cost of your education You do not need to pay your tuition and fees before coming to Wichita. Estimated expenses for the term are listed on your I-20. Tuition and fees may vary depending upon the number of hours in which you enroll (minimum 9 credit hours) and the types of courses. Cost per credit hour does change periodically and the most current amount will be posted on the website ( wichita.edu/tuition ). Upon arrival in Wichita, you will be expected to pay your tuition and fees , housing, books, and medical insurance. You will not be allowed to attend classes or live in a University residence hall without making arrangements to pay all of the above items. An exact amount of tuition and/or expenses cannot be quoted to the student prior to arrival. Graduate assistantship opportunities More than 700 graduate assistantships are awarded annually. These assistantships provide opportunities for teaching or research, a stipend, and benefits that may include tuition reduction and discounted health insurance. The actual dollar amount varies according to the employment length, number of hours worked per week, and the money available within the program area. Hiring for assistantships is handled by the individual departments. You should contact your academic advisor (listed on your admission letter) or the graduate coordinator of your area or program of interest. You are not restricted to working in the program to which you have been admitted. Please note: Assistantship offers for master's students prior to arrival on campus are rare. Most departments prefer the student complete at least one semester of study at WSU before being considered for a position. Payment options Tuition and fees payments are charged on a semester-by-semester basis. Deadline for payment is usually two weeks after school starts. There are several options to make payment to the university: Direct Deposit from U.S. Bank Account: After you open a bank account in the U.S., you can setup direct deposit from your U.S. bank account to your student account at WSU. Electronic Bank Transfer: Wichita State University has partnered with Flywire to streamline the process of international wire transfers. Please visit our website for more information: wichita.edu/pay Cash, Check, Bank Draft, Money Order, or Traveler's Checks: If you bring a check or bank draft with you to Wichita, it is very important that the check be made payable to "Wichita State University" (and not to you). Your check should include the address of the bank in the U.S. for collections. If the check is made payable to you, you may not be able to use the money for 1-2 weeks after the check is deposited to your bank in the U.S. If your check is for an amount that exceeds what you owe, any extra amount will be applied to your next semester's tuition and will not be refunded to you. Credit Card: If you use a credit card to pay for your tuition, fees, medical insurance, or housing, a nonrefundable 2.85% service fee will be added. Debit Card - VISA, MasterCard: Payment is made online only by going to the Student Account Suite . To avoid the 2.85% fee (min $3) associated with credit card payments, we encourage you to pay using electronic check process by entering the bank routing and account number attached to the debit card. Debit card payments cannot be made to a cashier in the Accounts Receivable office. Installment Payment Plan: This allows you to pay for your tuition and fees in smaller installments each semester. With this plan, you can make a nonrefundable payment of US$130 (which includes a US$30 administrative fee) before the payment deadline in each semester. After the initial payment of US$130, the balance will be split into three equal installments due on the 15th of each month. You can arrange the Payment Plan by logging into your WSU student account.

title: Visa Tips
text: Visa Tips - Apply Early! The visa wait time in many countries can be several weeks so apply early. | Visa Wait Times Apply for a visa up to 120 days before the start date on your I-20 or DS-2019. Pay the SEVIS Fee How to Apply for an F-1 Visa or J-1 Visa Documents Required for a Visa Interview Required Documents for a Visa Your local U.S. Embassy or Consulate may require additional documentation. Make sure your social media accounts are set to 'public'. This will help with the identity and admissibility checks required by U.S. law. During the Visa Interview Most visa interviews are only about 3 minutes long. During the interview, be honest, friendly, and organized. You must convince the visa officer that you are not trying to immigrate to the U.S. Be prepared to explain what companies in your country that you would like to work for after you finish your studies in the U.S. NEVER , NEVER , NEVER say that you would like to get permanent residency and remain in the U.S. after you graduate. You may be asked about what research you plan on doing while in your graduate program. It's important to be honest. Your program may not have a research component if you are pursuing an coursework only option. If you are doing a thesis option, tell them what you plan to research or are interested in. You will also want to be familiar with what your advisor's research area is. Visa officers often ask why you chose a specific major, why you chose to study at Wichita State, or why you chose to study in Wichita. You must be prepared to answer these questions. Information About Wichita State Information About Your Major Information About the City of Wichita Reasons for Visa Denials The most common reasons for visa denials are: The visa officer suspected the student of wanting to immigrate to the U.S. You must prove to the visa officer that you plan to return home after graduation. Examples of proof: Owning a house or business in your country Having a guaranteed job when you return home Having a spouse, children, or close family at home You will inherit property, a business, or assets in your country Have admission to a major that will allow you to get a job when you return home. For example, if you major in Aerospace Engineering, an aerospace industry must exist in your country so that you can find a job after you graduate. You do not have enough money to study in the U.S. You did not bring all required documents with you to the U.S. Embassy for the interview. You lied about something on your visa application or during the visa interview. You failed a security background check (called "Administrative Processing). You did not list your social media accounts. Help! I Was Denied a Visa! Visa Denial Help If you are denied a visa and would like to try again, you may need to request readmission for a future term and get a new I-20. No university in the U.S. can control the outcome of a visa application. We cannot require the embassy to grant you a visa or influence their decision in any way.

text: Information for International Graduate Applicants - Browse helpful information and resources for international students applying to graduate school at Wichita State University. We may be able to provide some assistance, please contact graduate.admissions@wichita.edu . Getting Started Virtual Tour Graduate Admissions Brochure STEM-designated degrees What is STEM? Department of Homeland Security maintains a complete list of fields that fall within the regulatory definition of "STEM field" that qualifies certain degrees to fulfill the extension requirement. This list is known as the STEM Designated Degree Program list. Learn more The Department of Education's Classification of Instructional Program (CIP) taxonomy system serves as the basis for the STEM OPT extension. Learn more about the STEM programs . The Graduate School at Wichita State University offers several STEM Designated Degree Programs and concentrations. In general, STEM programs will include fields involving research, innovation and/or development of new technologies using engineering, mathematics, natural sciences or computer science. Check out the STEM Programs that are being offered here: Aerospace Engineering Applied Mathematics Biological Sciences Biomedical Engineering Business Analytics Chemistry Computing Computer Science Data Science Earth, Environmental, and Physical Science Economics and Quantitative Analysis Electrical and Computer Engineering Engineering Management Exercise Science Industrial Engineering Innovation Design Management Science and Supply Chain Management Mathematics Mathematical Data Science Mechanical Engineering Materials Engineering Physics Global Select The Global Select scholarship is assessed once at the time of your admission. It is based on your GPA with the transcripts you provide at that time. If you are awarded the scholarship, you will be notified by email. If you are not awarded the scholarship, you will not be notified. Graduate Degree Programs Wichita State University offers the widest range of graduate degree choices in the area. See all graduate degrees Important Information for You Fee Waivers The Graduate School does not provide application fee waivers. All applicants are required to pay the fee in order to have their application processed and reviewed. U.S. Bachelor Equivalency When reviewing academic records from institutions outside the U.S., the university will determine whether an applicant's education is equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree. View a list of diplomas and certificates from various countries that may be considered equivalent . Application Status You can check the status of your application in your application portal . We cannot give you an estimated time of when a final decision will be made, however when there is an update to your status, your portal will reflect that. Application Materials Admission requirements are listed on the website for each graduate program. We ask that applicants not submit materials that are not required as it can hold up the application / review process. Programs Not Eligible Under F1 Visa Some programs are unable to meet the enrollment requirements necessary for F1 Visa eligibility. International students who wish to study on an F1 Visa at Wichita State University should apply to one of our other programs . To see if a program is eligible, refer to the list below: Arts Leadership & Management* Health Administration* Human Resource Management* Nursing School Psychology Special Education* Sport Management Teaching *These programs may be completed online. Decisions Depending on the program you apply for and the volume of applicants, decisions can take a few days to a few months. It's important to check your application portal for missing materials. When a decision is made on your application, you will receive an email to check your portal for the decision . Changing Majors / Switching Programs At the graduate level, you cannot simply notify us that you want to change your major. In order to get into a new program, you have to apply, submit the app fee, and be re-evaluated based on that programs admission requirements. Please be aware that the app fee amount is based on date and cannot be changed and certain programs have deadlines for application submission. Conditions / Pre-requisites If you have certain conditions or pre-requisite courses listed in our admission letter, the expectation is that you clear those within your first semester to first year as a graduate student. These were assigned to you based on the review the program did of your transcripts / marksheets. They are to help prepare you for the rigor of the graduate program and make sure you are successful in higher level coursework. If you think you should not have been assigned certain pre-requisite courses, please reach out to your academic advisor listed in your admission letter. English Proficiency It is mandatory for international applicants to provide an acceptable TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, or Duolingo score report for admission. We understand that many countries have English as an official language along with other languages that are native to that country. Many, if not most, of our foreign students are educated (at least at the college level) in English. However, we find that the experience of being educated in English vs. living in a country where the native language is English, to be very different. To ensure the success of our graduate students, we require demonstration of high level of proficiency in English. The only time the TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/Duolingo requirement is waived is when the applicant has graduated from a university located in the US/UK/Canadian/New Zealand, or Australia within the last 2 years. Testing English proficiency is not only to our benefit, but yours as well. It will help you measure your preparedness for reading, writing, and comprehending English at a level sufficient for a higher education setting. We want all of our students to be successful, and excellent English language skills are a key to that success. Graduate Assistantships Financial assistance for graduate students usually comes in the form of an assistantship with the department. Assistantships provide a wage and, if you work enough hours, may entitle you to a lower in-state tuition rate. Each department does its own hiring. You should contact the graduate coordinator of the department regarding assistantship opportunities, however Shocker Central is a great place to start looking. You can search and apply for on-campus employment via the Shocker Central website. Keep in mind that most departments will not consider a student for an assistantship until they have completed at least one semester of study at WSU. Assistantships are very competitive, so there is no guarantee you will be given an assistantship. Graduate Coordinators You'll contact your graduate coordinator whenever you have questions about courses or your degree program. There are a variety of reasons to contact your coordinator, including: Finding a program that's the right fit for you Knowing your program's prerequisites, core requisites, and optional electives before you start Learning more about the credit hour system How to register for classes Graduation options Questions If you have a question, please contact your coordinator by email. Contact your coordinator Visa Fee and Application Tips Helpful tips for obtaining your visa. Visa tips SEVIS Fee Information What is the SEVIS fee? The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) requires people who want F-1 or J-1 visas to pay a one-time SEVIS Fee before applying for a visa. Learn more The SEVIS Fee for F-1 visas is $350. The SEVIS fee for J-1 visas is $220. This is in addition to the normal visa application fee of US$185 and the visa integrity fee of $250. The SEVIS fee helps to pay for SEVIS (Student and Exchange Information System) that U.S. schools use to issue I-20 forms. How do I pay the SEVIS Fee? The SEVIS Fee can be paid to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) online, by mail with a check or money order, or by Western Union. To pay your SEVIS Fee, you must have: F-1 Visas: School Code for Wichita State University: KAN214F00668000 SEVIS Identification Number: Located above the bar code on the right side of your I-20 starting with "N" J-1 Visas: Program Code: P-1-01549 SEVIS Identification Number: Located on your DS-2019 To pay your SEVIS Fee, please go to the following website for complete details: https://www.fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html When must I pay the SEVIS Fee? The fee should be paid at least three business days before you apply for your visa, change of status, or reinstatement application. Pre-Departure Information Pay tuition and fees Pay Tuition and Fees Students are not required to pay their tuition and fees before coming to Wichita. Tuition, fees, and housing payments are charged on a semester-by-semester basis. Deadline for payment is usually two weeks after school starts. There are several options to make payment to the university: Direct Deposit from U.S. Bank Account: After you open a bank account in the U.S., you can setup direct deposit from your U.S. bank account to your student account at WSU.
